questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 1 | CE Q11
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Matrix P is given as
\[P = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \]
The TRUE option is
options: Trace of P is equal to the sum of the Eigen values of P.
\( P^T P \) is an identity matrix.
Absolute magnitude of each Eigen value is 1.

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: Trace of P is equal to the sum of the Eigen values of P.
structuredOptions.html: Trace of P is equal to the sum of the Eigen values of P.

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: \( P^T P \) is an identity matrix.
structuredOptions.html: \( P^T P \) is an identity matrix.

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: Absolute magnitude of each Eigen value is 1.
structuredOptions.html: Absolute magnitude of each Eigen value is 1.

questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis (Bloom's Level 4)
  • Given Data: \[P = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\]
  • Aim: Identify the mathematically true statement regarding matrix properties and Eigenvalues.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Trace Property: \(\text{Tr}(A) = \sum \lambda_i\) (sum of diagonal elements = sum of eigenvalues).
  • Orthogonality: \(P^T P = I\).
  • Skew-Symmetry: \(P^T = -P\) (requires zero diagonal).
  • Eigenvalues: Roots of \(|P - \lambda I| = 0\).

4. Solution Method:

Check the Trace property first (universal identity), then verify eigenvalues to rule out other options.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Verify Option (A) — Trace = Sum of Eigenvalues:
    \(\text{Tr}(P) = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3\). This is an inherent property of any square matrix. ✓
  2. Verify Option (B) — Orthogonality:
    Since \(P^T = P\):
    \[P^T P = P^2 = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \neq I\]
    Not orthogonal. ✗
  3. Verify Option (D) — Eigenvalues:
    \[|P - \lambda I| = 0 \implies (1-\lambda)[(1-\lambda)^2 - 1] = 0\]
    \[\implies \lambda(1-\lambda)(\lambda - 2) = 0\]
    Eigenvalues: \(\lambda = 0, 1, 2\). Absolute magnitudes are not all 1. ✗

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Trace = Sum of Eigenvalues is a fundamental matrix property.  |  Correct option: (A)

The above system of equations represents a
questions.explanation:

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis (Bloom's Level 4)
  • Given Data: Homogeneous system \(AX = 0\) where \[A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}, \quad X = \begin{Bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{Bmatrix}\]
  • Aim: Determine the geometric representation of the solution set in 3D space.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Rank (\(r\)): Number of linearly independent rows.
  • Nullity (\(k\)): \(n - r\), dimension of the solution space.
  • Geometry: Nullity 1 = Line; Nullity 2 = Plane; Nullity 0 = Point (Origin).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Find Rank of \(A\):

    Both rows are non-zero and linearly independent. \(\text{Rank}(A) = 2\).
  2. Calculate Nullity:
    \(n = 3\), \(\text{Nullity} = 3 - 2 = 1\).
  3. Geometric Interpretation:
    A 1-dimensional solution space in \(\mathbb{R}^3\) corresponds to a line passing through the origin.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: The solution set is a line through the origin.  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 1 | CE Q26
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Bag I contains 4 white and 6 black balls.
Bag II contains 4 white and 3 black balls.
One ball is drawn at random from any one of the two bags and it is found to be a black ball. The probability that the black ball was drawn from Bag I is _______
(rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability (Bayes' Theorem)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Bag I: 4 White, 6 Black (Total = 10)
    • Bag II: 4 White, 3 Black (Total = 7)
    • Event: A black ball is drawn.
  • Aim: Find the probability the drawn black ball came from Bag I.

3. Core Concepts:

Bayes' Theorem:

\[P(E_1|B) = \dfrac{P(B|E_1) \cdot P(E_1)}{P(B|E_1) \cdot P(E_1) + P(B|E_2) \cdot P(E_2)}\]

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Initial Probabilities: \(P(E_1) = P(E_2) = \dfrac{1}{2}\)
  2. Conditional Probabilities:
    \(P(B|E_1) = \dfrac{6}{10} = \dfrac{3}{5}\); \(\quad P(B|E_2) = \dfrac{3}{7}\)
  3. Total Probability:
    \[P(B) = \dfrac{3}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{3}{7} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{10} + \dfrac{3}{14} = \dfrac{21+15}{70} = \dfrac{36}{70} = \dfrac{18}{35}\]
  4. Apply Bayes' Theorem:
    \[P(E_1|B) = \dfrac{3/10}{18/35} = \dfrac{3}{10} \times \dfrac{35}{18} = \dfrac{7}{12} \approx 0.5833\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.58  |  Accepted key range: 0.50 to 0.66

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 1 | CE Q27
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
A matrix is given as:
\[\begin{bmatrix} 9 & 15 \\ 15 & 50 \end{bmatrix} \]
By performing Cholesky decomposition, \( |l_{22}| \) of the lower triangular matrix is _______
(in integer).
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Cholesky Decomposition)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: \[A = \begin{bmatrix} 9 & 15 \\ 15 & 50 \end{bmatrix}\]
  • Aim: Find \(|l_{22}|\) after Cholesky decomposition.

3. Core Concepts:

Cholesky Decomposition: \(A = L \cdot L^T\) where \(L = \begin{bmatrix} l_{11} & 0 \\ l_{21} & l_{22} \end{bmatrix}\)

\[L \cdot L^T = \begin{bmatrix} l_{11}^2 & l_{11}l_{21} \\ l_{11}l_{21} & l_{21}^2 + l_{22}^2 \end{bmatrix}\]

Sanity check: \(\det(A) = 9 \times 50 - 15^2 = 225 > 0\) → matrix is positive definite, decomposition is valid.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. \(l_{11}^2 = 9 \implies l_{11} = 3\)
  2. \(l_{11} \cdot l_{21} = 15 \implies 3 \cdot l_{21} = 15 \implies l_{21} = 5\)
  3. \(l_{21}^2 + l_{22}^2 = 50 \implies 25 + l_{22}^2 = 50 \implies l_{22}^2 = 25 \implies l_{22} = \pm 5\)
  4. \(|l_{22}| = 5\)

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 5  |  Accepted key range: 5 to 5

questions.question:
It is given that \( x \) and \( y \) are integers in the following equation:
\[(x + y - 7)^2 + (y + 3x - 13)^2 = 0 \]
The value of \( (x^3 + y^3) \) is _______
(in integer).
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Algebra

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: \((x + y - 7)^2 + (y + 3x - 13)^2 = 0\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are integers.
  • Aim: Find the value of \(x^3 + y^3\).

3. Core Concepts:

For real numbers \(A\) and \(B\): \(A^2 + B^2 = 0 \iff A = 0 \text{ and } B = 0\)

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Set up linear equations:
    \[x + y = 7 \quad \cdots (1)\]
    \[3x + y = 13 \quad \cdots (2)\]
  2. Subtract (1) from (2):
    \[2x = 6 \implies x = 3\]
  3. Substitute into (1):
    \[y = 7 - 3 = 4\]
  4. Evaluate:
    \[x^3 + y^3 = 3^3 + 4^3 = 27 + 64 = 91\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 91  |  Accepted key range: 91 to 91

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 1 | CE Q36
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Let \( f(x) \) be a continuous function defined in \( [0,2] \rightarrow \mathbb{R} \) and satisfying the equation
\[ \int_{0}^{2} f(x)[x - f(x)]dx = \dfrac{2}{3}. \]
The value of \( f(1) \) is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • A continuous function \(f(x)\) defined in \([0,2] \rightarrow \mathbb{R}\)
    • Integral equation: \(\int_0^2 f(x)[x - f(x)]\,dx = \dfrac{2}{3}\)
  • Aim: Find the value of \(f(1)\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Definite Integrals & Properties: Expanding and manipulating integrals of polynomials and functions.
  • Completing the Square: For an integrand of the form \(ax - a^2\), we can rewrite it as \(\dfrac{x^2}{4} - \left(a - \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^2\).
  • Zero-Integral Property: If \(g(x) \ge 0\) for all \(x \in [a,b]\), and \(\int_a^b g(x)\,dx = 0\), then \(g(x) = 0\) everywhere in \([a,b]\) for a continuous function \(g\).

4. Solution Method:

We are given an integral equation involving \(f(x)\) and \((f(x))^2\). We expand the integrand and form a perfect square involving \(f(x)\) and \(x\). By evaluating the independent \(x^2\) term over the same limits, we notice a mathematical identity that forces the squared term to be zero.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Expand the integral:
    \[\int_0^2 \left[x f(x) - (f(x))^2 \right] dx = \dfrac{2}{3}\]
  2. Complete the square for the integrand:
    \[-(f(x))^2 + x f(x) = -\left((f(x))^2 - x f(x)\right)\]
    Add and subtract \(\dfrac{x^2}{4}\) inside the parentheses:
    \[= \dfrac{x^2}{4} - \left(f(x) - \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^2\]
  3. Substitute back into the integral:
    \[\int_0^2 \left[\dfrac{x^2}{4} - \left(f(x) - \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^2 \right] dx = \dfrac{2}{3}\]
  4. Evaluate the known integral part:
    \[\int_0^2 \dfrac{x^2}{4}\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x^3}{12}\right]_0^2 = \dfrac{8}{12} = \dfrac{2}{3}\]
  5. Simplify the main equation:
    \[\dfrac{2}{3} - \int_0^2 \left(f(x) - \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^2 dx = \dfrac{2}{3}\]
    \[\int_0^2 \left(f(x) - \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^2 dx = 0\]
  6. Deduce the function \(f(x)\):
    Since \(\left(f(x) - \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^2 \ge 0\), the integral equals zero only if the integrand is zero everywhere:
    \[f(x) = \dfrac{x}{2} \quad \text{for all } x \in [0,2]\]
  7. Calculate \(f(1)\):
    \[f(1) = \dfrac{1}{2}\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{1}{2}\)  |  Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 1 | CE Q37
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
An ordinary differential equation is given below.
\[x^2 \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 6y \]
Considering \( a \) and \( b \) as arbitrary constants, the general solution of the equation is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Differential Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Ordinary differential equation: \(x^2 \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 6y\)
    • \(a\) and \(b\) are arbitrary constants.
  • Aim: Find the general solution \(y(x)\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Cauchy-Euler Equation: A linear homogeneous ODE of the form \(a_n x^n \dfrac{d^n y}{dx^n} + \cdots + a_1 x \dfrac{dy}{dx} + a_0 y = 0\).
  • Trial Solution: For Cauchy-Euler equations, we assume a solution of the form \(y = x^m\).

4. Solution Method:

Rewrite the equation in standard homogeneous form \(x^2 y'' - 6y = 0\). Substitute the trial solution \(y = x^m\), extract the auxiliary/characteristic equation in terms of \(m\), find the roots, and construct the general solution.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Assume trial solution:
    Let \(y = x^m\), then \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = m x^{m-1}\) and \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = m(m-1)x^{m-2}\).
  2. Substitute into the ODE:
    \[x^2 \cdot m(m-1)x^{m-2} = 6x^m\]
    \[m(m-1)x^m = 6x^m\]
    Dividing by \(x^m\) (assuming \(x \neq 0\)):
    \[m(m-1) = 6\]
  3. Solve the characteristic equation:
    \[m^2 - m - 6 = 0\]
    \[(m-3)(m+2) = 0\]
    Roots: \(m_1 = 3\) and \(m_2 = -2\).
  4. Formulate the general solution:
    Since the roots are real and distinct:
    \[y(x) = ax^3 + bx^{-2} = ax^3 + \dfrac{b}{x^2}\]
    (where \(a\) and \(b\) are arbitrary constants).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(y(x) = ax^3 + \dfrac{b}{x^2}\)  |  Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 1 | CE Q48
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Starting with the first approximation as \( x = 0.5 \), the second approximation for the root of the following function by the Newton-Raphson method is _______
(rounded off to two decimal places).
\[f(x) = e^{-x} - x \]
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Objective function: \(f(x) = e^{-x} - x\)
    • Initial guess: \(x_0 = 0.5\)
  • Aim: Find the second approximation (\(x_1\)) using the Newton-Raphson method.

3. Core Concepts:

Newton-Raphson Method: An iterative root-finding algorithm:

\[x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}\]

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Find the derivative:
    \[f(x) = e^{-x} - x \implies f'(x) = -e^{-x} - 1\]
  2. Evaluate at \(x_0 = 0.5\):
    \[f(0.5) = e^{-0.5} - 0.5 \approx 0.60653 - 0.5 = 0.10653\]
    \[f'(0.5) = -e^{-0.5} - 1 \approx -0.60653 - 1 = -1.60653\]
  3. Apply Newton-Raphson formula:
    \[x_1 = 0.5 - \dfrac{0.10653}{-1.60653} = 0.5 + 0.06631 = 0.56631\]
  4. Round to two decimal places:
    \[x_1 \approx 0.57\]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.57  |  Accepted key range: 0.55 to 0.58

Values of \( y \) for different values of \( x \) are tabulated below.
x-212
y28416

If a second-degree interpolating polynomial \( P_2(x) \) is used to represent \( y \), the value of \( P_2(0) \) is _______
(rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Three coordinate points: \((-2,\, 28)\), \((1,\, 4)\), \((2,\, 16)\).
  • Aim: Construct a second-degree polynomial \(P_2(x)\) and determine its y-intercept, \(P_2(0)\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Polynomial Interpolation: For 3 distinct points, a unique parabola of the form \(P_2(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) can be fitted.
  • Finding \(P_2(0)\) simply means finding the constant term \(c\).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Set up the system of linear equations:
    For \(x=-2,\, y=28\):
    \[4a - 2b + c = 28 \quad \cdots (1)\]
    For \(x=1,\, y=4\):
    \[a + b + c = 4 \quad \cdots (2)\]
    For \(x=2,\, y=16\):
    \[4a + 2b + c = 16 \quad \cdots (3)\]
  2. Solve for \(b\):
    Subtract (3) from (1):
    \[-4b = 12 \implies b = -3\]
  3. Solve for \(a\) and \(c\):
    Substituting \(b = -3\) into (2): \(a + c = 7 \quad \cdots (4)\)
    Substituting \(b = -3\) into (3): \(4a + c = 22 \quad \cdots (5)\)
    Subtract (4) from (5): \(3a = 15 \implies a = 5\)
    From (4): \(c = 7 - 5 = 2\)
  4. Evaluate \(P_2(0)\):
    \[P_2(0) = c = 2\]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2  |  Accepted key range: 2 to 2

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q11
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: Matrix A has the eigenvalues 1, 2, and 3. The Trace of \( \mathbf{A}^2 \) is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension & Application
  • Given Data: Eigenvalues of Matrix \(A\): \(\lambda_1 = 1,\ \lambda_2 = 2,\ \lambda_3 = 3\)
  • Aim: Find the Trace of the matrix \(A^2\).

3. Core Concepts:

Eigenvalue Power Property: If a square matrix \(A\) has eigenvalues \(\lambda\), then the matrix \(A^k\) (where \(k\) is an integer) will have eigenvalues \(\lambda^k\).

Trace of a Matrix: The trace of any square matrix is fundamentally equal to the sum of its eigenvalues.\[\text{Trace}(A) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \lambda_i \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the eigenvalues of the matrix \(A^2\) using the power property.
  2. Sum these newly found eigenvalues to calculate the trace of \(A^2\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate eigenvalues of \(A^2\):
    Given \(\lambda_A = \{1, 2, 3\}\). The eigenvalues for \(A^2\) will be:
    • \(\lambda_1^2 = 1^2 = 1\)
    • \(\lambda_2^2 = 2^2 = 4\)
    • \(\lambda_3^2 = 3^2 = 9\)
  2. Calculate the Trace of \(A^2\):
    \[\text{Trace}(A^2) = \lambda_1^2 + \lambda_2^2 + \lambda_3^2 \]\[\text{Trace}(A^2) = 1 + 4 + 9 = 14 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 14 | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q12
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
A fifth-degree polynomial in \( x \) is defined for \( x > 0 \). All coefficients of the polynomial are positive. The first derivative of the polynomial is obtained numerically at a point by using the first-order forward as well as the first-order backward difference methods. Identical step lengths are used for both the methods.

Following statements are made.
(I) Forward difference method underestimates the true derivative.
(II) Backward difference method overestimates the true derivative.

Which one of the following options is CORRECT?
options: Statement (I) is TRUE and statement (II) is FALSE.
Statement (I) is FALSE and statement (II) is TRUE.

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Statement (I) is TRUE and statement (II) is FALSE.
structuredOptions.html: Statement (I) is TRUE and statement (II) is FALSE.

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: Statement (I) is FALSE and statement (II) is TRUE.
structuredOptions.html: Statement (I) is FALSE and statement (II) is TRUE.

questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • \(P(x)\): 5th-degree polynomial for \(x > 0\).
    • All coefficients are strictly positive (\(a_i > 0\)).
    • Derivatives obtained numerically via first-order forward and backward difference methods.
  • Aim: Evaluate validity of Statements (I) and (II) regarding whether these methods under/overestimate the true first derivative.

3. Core Concepts:

Function behavior: For \(P(x) = a_5x^5 + a_4x^4 + a_3x^3 + a_2x^2 + a_1x + a_0\) with all \(a_i > 0\) and \(x > 0\), the second derivative \(P''(x)\) is strictly positive. A positive second derivative means the function is strictly convex (concave upward).

Taylor Series Expansion:
Forward Step: \(f(x+h) = f(x) + hf'(x) + \dfrac{h^2}{2}f''(\xi_1)\)
Backward Step: \(f(x-h) = f(x) - hf'(x) + \dfrac{h^2}{2}f''(\xi_2)\)

4. Solution Method:

By manipulating the Taylor expansions, we can find expressions for the numerical derivatives and compare them directly to the exact analytical derivative \(f'(x)\). The sign of the truncation error (which depends on \(f''(x)\)) dictates whether it's an overestimate or underestimate.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Evaluate Forward Difference Method:
    From Taylor series:\[\dfrac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = f'(x) + \dfrac{h}{2}f''(\xi_1) \]Since \(f''(x) > 0\) for all \(x > 0\), the error term \(\dfrac{h}{2}f''(\xi_1)\) is positive.
    Therefore, Forward Difference value \(>\) True \(f'(x)\).
    Conclusion: Forward difference overestimates the true derivative. (Statement I says it underestimates → FALSE).
  2. Evaluate Backward Difference Method:
    From Taylor series:\[\dfrac{f(x) - f(x-h)}{h} = f'(x) - \dfrac{h}{2}f''(\xi_2) \]Since \(f''(x) > 0\), the term being subtracted \(\dfrac{h}{2}f''(\xi_2)\) is positive.
    Therefore, Backward Difference value \(<\) True \(f'(x)\).
    Conclusion: Backward difference underestimates the true derivative. (Statement II says it overestimates → FALSE).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Both statements (I) and (II) are FALSE | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q13
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Periodic function \( f(x) \) is given below.
\[f(x) = \begin{cases} -1, & \text{when } -\pi < x < 0 \\ 1, & \text{when } 0 < x < \pi \end{cases} ; f(x + 2\pi) = f(x) \]
The CORRECT option representing the Fourier series expansion of \( f(x) \) is:
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus (Fourier Series)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • \(f(x) = -1\) for \(-\pi < x < 0\)
    • \(f(x) = 1\) for \(0 < x < \pi\)
    • Period \(T = 2\pi\)
  • Aim: Determine the CORRECT Fourier series expansion for \(f(x)\).

3. Core Concepts:

Symmetry (Odd/Even Functions): Since \(f(-x) = -f(x)\), the function is odd.

Fourier Coefficients for Odd Functions:

  • \(a_0 = 0\)
  • \(a_n = 0\) (No cosine terms)
  • \(b_n = \dfrac{2}{L} \int_{0}^{L} f(x) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{L}\right) dx\), where \(L = \pi\) (half-period).

4. Solution Method:

Compute the \(b_n\) coefficients integrating over \(0\) to \(\pi\) where \(f(x) = 1\), and construct the sine series.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Formula Setup for \(b_n\):\[b_n = \dfrac{2}{\pi} \int_{0}^{\pi} (1) \cdot \sin(nx)\, dx \]
  2. Integration:\[ b_n = \dfrac{2}{\pi} \left[\dfrac{-\cos(nx)}{n} \right]_{0}^{\pi} \]\[ b_n = \dfrac{-2}{n\pi}[\cos(n\pi) - \cos(0)] \]Recall that \(\cos(n\pi) = (-1)^n\) and \(\cos(0) = 1\).\[ b_n = \dfrac{-2}{n\pi}[(-1)^n - 1] = \dfrac{2}{n\pi}[1 - (-1)^n] \]
  3. Evaluate for Even and Odd \(n\):
    • If \(n\) is even (2, 4, 6, ...): \(1 - (1) = 0 \Rightarrow b_n = 0\)
    • If \(n\) is odd (1, 3, 5, ...): \(1 - (-1) = 2 \Rightarrow b_n = \dfrac{4}{n\pi}\)
  4. Construct the Series:\[f(x) = \sum_{n=1,3,5}^{\infty} \dfrac{4}{n\pi} \sin(nx) \]\[ f(x) = \dfrac{4}{\pi} \left[\sin x + \dfrac{\sin 3x}{3} + \dfrac{\sin 5x}{5} + \cdots \right] \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(f(x) = \dfrac{4}{\pi} \left[\sin x + \dfrac{\sin 3x}{3} + \cdots \right]\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q30
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
A partial differential equation is given below.
\[\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} - \dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2} = 0 \]
Possible solution(s) is/are:
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Partial Differential Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: PDE: \(\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} - \dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2} = 0\)
  • Aim: Identify the possible solution(s) from the given MSQ options.

3. Core Concepts:

This is the standard 1D wave equation \(u_{xx} - u_{yy} = 0\) (with \(c^2 = 1\)).
D'Alembert's general solution states that any function of the form \(u(x,y) = f(x+y) + g(x-y)\) will satisfy this PDE.

4. Solution Method:

Check each option by computing second partial derivatives \(u_{xx}\) and \(u_{yy}\) and verifying whether \(u_{xx} - u_{yy} = 0\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • (A) \(u = (x+y)^5\):
    \(u_{xx} = 20(x+y)^3\), \(u_{yy} = 20(x+y)^3\)
    \[u_{xx} - u_{yy} = 0 \quad \checkmark \text{ (Correct)} \]
  • (B) \(u = (x-2y)^3\):
    \(u_{xx} = 6(x-2y)\), \(u_{yy} = 24(x-2y)\)
    \[u_{xx} - u_{yy} \neq 0 \quad \times \text{ (Incorrect)} \]
  • (C) \(u = \cos(x+y)\):
    \(u_{xx} = -\cos(x+y)\), \(u_{yy} = -\cos(x+y)\)
    \[u_{xx} - u_{yy} = 0 \quad \checkmark \text{ (Correct)} \]
  • (D) \(u = \sin(x-2y)\):
    \(u_{xx} = -\sin(x-2y)\), \(u_{yy} = -4\sin(x-2y)\)
    \[u_{xx} - u_{yy} \neq 0 \quad \times \text{ (Incorrect)} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \((x+y)^5\) and \(\cos(x+y)\) | Correct options: (A) and (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q31
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
The eigenvalues of \( [A] = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -3.5 & 6 \\ 3.5 & 5 & 2 \\ 8 & 1 & 8.5 \end{bmatrix} \) are
\( \lambda_1 = -1.547, \lambda_2 = 12.330, \text{ and } \lambda_3 = 4.711 \).
The absolute value of the determinant of matrix A is ______ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: A \(3 \times 3\) matrix \(A\) with eigenvalues \(\lambda_1 = -1.547\), \(\lambda_2 = 12.330\), \(\lambda_3 = 4.711\).
    \[A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -3.5 & 6 \\ 3.5 & 5 & 2 \\ 8 & 1 & 8.5 \end{bmatrix} \]
  • Aim: Find the absolute value of the determinant of matrix \(A\) (rounded to 2 decimal places).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Determinant Property: \(\det(A) = \lambda_1 \times \lambda_2 \times \lambda_3\).
  • Computing the determinant directly from matrix elements avoids intermediate rounding biases in the provided eigenvalues.

4. Solution Method:

Calculate the exact determinant via Laplace expansion along Row 1, then compute its absolute value.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Expand along Row 1:\[ \det(A) = 2[(5)(8.5)-(2)(1)] - (-3.5)[(3.5)(8.5)-(2)(8)] + 6[(3.5)(1)-(5)(8)] \]
  2. Compute minor brackets:
    • First minor: \(42.5 - 2 = 40.5\)
    • Second minor: \(29.75 - 16 = 13.75\)
    • Third minor: \(3.5 - 40 = -36.5\)
  3. Evaluate the full expression:\[\det(A) = 2(40.5) + 3.5(13.75) + 6(-36.5) \]\[\det(A) = 81 + 48.125 - 219 = -89.875 \]
  4. Find the absolute value:\[|\det(A)| = |-89.875| = 89.875 \approx 89.88 \]

Note: Calculating via eigenvalue product yields \(|-1.547 \times 12.330 \times 4.711| = 89.86\). Both values fall within the accepted answer key range.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 89.88 | Accepted key range: 89.00 to 91.00

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q36
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Let \( f(x) = \begin{vmatrix} x^3 & \sin x & \cos x \\ 6 & -1 & 0 \\ p & p^2 & p^3 \end{vmatrix} \)
where \( p \) is a constant.
The value of \( \dfrac{d^3}{dx^3}f(x) \) at \( x = 0 \) is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus & Linear Algebra

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:\[f(x) = \begin{vmatrix} x^3 & \sin x & \cos x \\ 6 & -1 & 0 \\ p & p^2 & p^3 \end{vmatrix} \]
  • Aim: Find the value of \(\dfrac{d^3}{dx^3}f(x)\) evaluated at \(x = 0\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Expansion of Determinants: A \(3 \times 3\) determinant can be expanded along any row or column.
  • Differentiation of Determinants: A determinant is differentiated by differentiating one row at a time while keeping the others constant.
  • Standard Derivatives: \(\dfrac{d^3}{dx^3}(x^3) = 6\), \(\dfrac{d^3}{dx^3}(\sin x) = -\cos x\), \(\dfrac{d^3}{dx^3}(\cos x) = \sin x\).

4. Solution Method:

Since the second and third rows contain only constants (with respect to \(x\)), their derivatives are zero. Thus, the third derivative of the entire determinant is simply the determinant with its first row differentiated three times.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Apply the third derivative to the first row:\[f'''(x) = \begin{vmatrix} 6 & -\cos x & \sin x \\ 6 & -1 & 0 \\ p & p^2 & p^3 \end{vmatrix} \]
  2. Substitute \(x = 0\):  \(\cos(0) = 1\),  \(\sin(0) = 0\):\[f'''(0) = \begin{vmatrix} 6 & -1 & 0 \\ 6 & -1 & 0 \\ p & p^2 & p^3 \end{vmatrix} \]
  3. Evaluate the resulting determinant:
    Row 1 (\(R_1\)) and Row 2 (\(R_2\)) are identical \((6,\ -1,\ 0)\). By the property of determinants, if any two rows are identical, the determinant equals exactly \(0\).\[f'''(0) = 0 \]Since the result is exactly \(0\), it is completely independent of \(p\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Independent of \(p\) | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q37
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Vector field \( \vec{V} \) is defined as
\[\vec{V} = 3x^2yz \hat{i} - 5xy \hat{j} + 6yz^2 \hat{k} \]
The curl of \( \vec{V} \) at point (2,-1,1) is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Vector Calculus

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Vector field \(\vec{V} = 3x^2yz\,\hat{i} - 5xy\,\hat{j} + 6yz^2\,\hat{k}\)
  • Aim: Compute the curl of \(\vec{V}\) (\( abla imes \vec{V}\)) at the point \((2, -1, 1)\).

3. Core Concepts:

Curl of a Vector Field: Represents the infinitesimal rotation of a 3D vector field.\[ abla imes \vec{V} = egin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \ \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z} \ V_x & V_y & V_z \end{vmatrix} \]

4. Solution Method:

Expand the cross product determinant to find the algebraic expression for the curl, then substitute \((x, y, z) = (2, -1, 1)\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Compute partial derivatives for each component:
    • \(\hat{i}\) component:\(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(6yz^2) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(-5xy) = 6z^2 - 0 = 6z^2\)
    • \(\hat{j}\) component:\(-\left(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(6yz^2) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(3x^2yz) ight) = -(0 - 3x^2y) = 3x^2y\)
    • \(\hat{k}\) component:\(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(-5xy) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(3x^2yz) = -5y - 3x^2z\)
    \[ abla imes \vec{V} = 6z^2\,\hat{i} + 3x^2y\,\hat{j} - (5y + 3x^2z)\,\hat{k} \]
  2. Substitute \((x, y, z) = (2, -1, 1)\):
    • \(\hat{i}\): \(6(1)^2 = 6\)
    • \(\hat{j}\): \(3(2)^2(-1) = -12\)
    • \(\hat{k}\): \(-[5(-1) + 3(4)(1)] = -[-5 + 12] = -7\)

Resultant vector: \(6\hat{i} - 12\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}\)

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(6\hat{i} - 12\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q46
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Consider differential equation \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} + xy = x \) with the condition as \( y = 0 \) at \( x = 0 \).
The value of \( y \) at \( x = 1.0 \) is ______ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Differential Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Differential Equation: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + xy = x\)
    • Boundary Condition: \(y = 0\) at \(x = 0\)
  • Aim: Find the value of \(y\) at \(x = 1.0\) (rounded to two decimal places).

3. Core Concepts:

  • First-Order Linear ODE: Standard form: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x)\)
  • Integrating Factor (IF): \(IF = e^{\int P(x)\,dx}\)
  • General Solution: \(y \cdot (IF) = \int Q(x) \cdot (IF)\,dx + C\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Identify \(P(x)\) and \(Q(x)\).
  2. Compute the Integrating Factor.
  3. Integrate to find the general solution.
  4. Apply the boundary condition to find constant \(C\).
  5. Evaluate \(y(1.0)\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify: \(P(x) = x\), \(Q(x) = x\)
  2. Integrating Factor:\[IF = e^{\int x\,dx} = e^{x^2/2} \]
  3. General Solution:\[y \cdot e^{x^2/2} = \int x \cdot e^{x^2/2}\,dx + C \]Let \(u = \dfrac{x^2}{2} \Rightarrow du = x\,dx\):\[y \cdot e^{x^2/2} = e^{x^2/2} + C \]Dividing by \(e^{x^2/2}\):\[y(x) = 1 + Ce^{-x^2/2} \]
  4. Apply Boundary Condition (\(y = 0\) at \(x = 0\)):\[0 = 1 + C \implies C = -1 \]Specific solution: \(y(x) = 1 - e^{-x^2/2}\)
  5. Evaluate at \(x = 1.0\):\[y(1.0) = 1 - e^{-0.5} = 1 - 0.6065 = 0.3935 \approx 0.39 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.39 | Accepted key range: 0.37 to 0.42

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q47
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
The age (in years) of a population is normally distributed with a mean of 36 and standard deviation of 12. The height (in cm) of the same population is also normally distributed with a mean of 160 and standard deviation of 10.
If the probability of age greater than 50 years is equal to the probability of height greater than \( h \), the value of \( h \) (in cm) is ______ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability & Statistics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Age distribution: \(A \sim N(\mu_A = 36,\ \sigma_A = 12)\)
    • Height distribution: \(H \sim N(\mu_H = 160,\ \sigma_H = 10)\)
    • Condition: \(P(A > 50) = P(H > h)\)
  • Aim: Find the value of height \(h\) in cm (rounded to two decimal places).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Standardization: Any normal variate \(X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)\) is converted to standard normal using:\[Z = \dfrac{X - \mu}{\sigma} \]
  • If \(P(A > x_1) = P(H > x_2)\), their corresponding \(Z\)-scores must be equal.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the \(Z\)-score for Age \(= 50\).
  2. Set this equal to the \(Z\)-score formula for Height \(= h\).
  3. Solve for \(h\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. \(Z\)-score for Age \(= 50\):\[Z_A = \dfrac{50 - 36}{12} = \dfrac{14}{12} = \dfrac{7}{6} \]
  2. Equate to \(Z\)-score for Height \(= h\):\[\dfrac{h - 160}{10} = \dfrac{7}{6} \]
  3. Solve for \(h\):\[h - 160 = 10 \times \dfrac{7}{6} = \dfrac{70}{6} = 11.6667 \]\[h = 160 + 11.6667 = 171.67\text{ cm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 171.67 cm | Accepted key range: 170.00 to 173.00

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q11
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: Suppose \(\lambda\) is an eigenvalue of matrix \(A\) and \(x\) is the corresponding eigenvector. Let \(x\) also be an eigenvector of the matrix \(B = A - 2I\), where \(I\) is the identity matrix. Then, the eigenvalue of \(B\) corresponding to the eigenvector \(x\) is equal to
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra / Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: 3. Application
  • Given Data: Matrix \(A\) has an eigenvalue \(\lambda\) with the corresponding eigenvector \(x\). Matrix \(B = A - 2I\), where \(I\) is the identity matrix.
  • Aim: Find the eigenvalue of matrix \(B\) corresponding to the eigenvector \(x\).

3. Core Concepts:

Eigenvalue Equation: For a square matrix \(A\), an eigenvector \(x\) and its corresponding eigenvalue \(\lambda\) satisfy the equation: \(Ax = \lambda x\).

Matrix Polynomials: If \(\lambda\) is an eigenvalue of \(A\), then for any scalar \(k\), the matrix \((A - kI)\) will have an eigenvalue of \((\lambda - k)\) corresponding to the exact same eigenvector \(x\).

4. Solution Method:

  • We start with the fundamental eigenvalue equation for matrix \(B\).
  • Substitute \(B = A - 2I\) and apply matrix distribution.
  • Substitute \(Ax\) with \(\lambda x\) and factor out the eigenvector \(x\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Write the eigenvalue equation for \(B\):
    \[Bx = (A - 2I)x \]
  2. Distribute the vector \(x\) inside the parenthesis:
    \[Bx = Ax - 2Ix \]
  3. Since \(I\) is the identity matrix, \(Ix = x\). Also, from the given data, \(Ax = \lambda x\). Substitute these into the equation:
    \[Bx = \lambda x - 2x \]
  4. Factor out the common vector \(x\):
    \[Bx = (\lambda - 2)x \]
  5. By definition, since \(Bx = \text{scalar} \cdot x\), the scalar \((\lambda - 2)\) is the eigenvalue of matrix \(B\) corresponding to the eigenvector \(x\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\lambda - 2\) | Option(s): D

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q12
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: Let \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \\ -2 & -3 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(b = \begin{bmatrix} b_1 \\ b_2 \\ b_3 \end{bmatrix}\). For \(Ax = b\) to be solvable, which one of the following options is the correct condition on \(b_1, b_2\), and \(b_3\):
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra / System of Linear Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: 4. Analysis & Synthesis
  • Given Data: Coefficient matrix \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \\ -2 & -3 \end{bmatrix}\)
    Constant vector \(b = \begin{bmatrix} b_1 \\ b_2 \\ b_3 \end{bmatrix}\)
  • Aim: Determine the algebraic condition on \(b_1, b_2, \text{ and } b_3\) for the system \(Ax = b\) to be consistent (solvable).

3. Core Concepts:

Rouché-Capelli Theorem: A system of linear equations \(Ax = b\) is solvable (consistent) if and only if the rank of the coefficient matrix \(A\) is equal to the rank of the augmented matrix \([A|b]\).

Row Echelon Form: Applying elementary row operations to reduce the augmented matrix helps identify conditions required to maintain equal ranks.

4. Solution Method:

  • Construct the augmented matrix \([A|b]\).
  • Perform Gaussian elimination (elementary row operations) to convert matrix \(A\) into an upper triangular form.
  • Since \(A\) has dimensions \(3 \times 2\), its maximum rank is 2. The 3rd row of the reduced matrix \(A\) will become strictly zeros.
  • For the system to be solvable, the corresponding 3rd row entry in the constant vector column must also equate to zero.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Form the augmented matrix:
    \[ [A|b] = \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 1 & b_1 \\ 1 & 3 & b_2 \\ -2 & -3 & b_3 \end{array}\right] \]
  2. Eliminate the entries below the pivot in the first column:
    \(R_2 \to R_2 - R_1\)
    \(R_3 \to R_3 + 2R_1\)
    \[ [A|b] = \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 1 & b_1 \\ 0 & 2 & b_2 - b_1 \\ 0 & -1 & b_3 + 2b_1 \end{array}\right] \]
  3. Eliminate the entry below the pivot in the second column to create a row of zeros in the coefficient side:
    \(R_3 \to 2R_3 + R_2\)
    \(R_3 \text{ transformation:} \quad 2(0) + 0 = 0 \quad | \quad 2(-1) + 2 = 0 \quad | \quad 2(b_3 + 2b_1) + (b_2 - b_1)\)
    \[ [A|b] = \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 1 & b_1 \\ 0 & 2 & b_2 - b_1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4b_1 + 2b_3 + b_2 - b_1 \end{array}\right] \]
  4. Simplify the expression in the \(3^{rd}\) row, constant column:
    \[3b_1 + b_2 + 2b_3 \]
  5. For the system to be solvable, rank(\(A\)) = rank(\([A|b]\)), thus the term corresponding to the zero-row must be zero:
    \[3b_1 + b_2 + 2b_3 = 0 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(3b_1 + b_2 + 2b_3 = 0\) | Option(s): B

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q13
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Which one of the following options is the correct Fourier series of the periodic function \(f(x)\) described below:

\( f(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } -2 < x < -1 \\ 2k & \text{if } -1 < x < 1 \\ 0 & \text{if } 1 < x < 2 \end{cases} \);  period = 4
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus / Fourier Series

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: 3. Application
  • Given Data: \(f(x) = 0\) for \(-2 < x < -1\)
    \(f(x) = 2k\) for \(-1 < x < 1\)
    \(f(x) = 0\) for \(1 < x < 2\)
    Period \(T = 4\)
  • Aim: Identify the correct Fourier series expansion for the periodic function \(f(x)\).

3. Core Concepts:

Fourier Series Representation: \(f(x) = \dfrac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{L}\right) + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{L}\right)\)

Half-Period (\(L\)): \(T = 2L \implies L = 2\).

Even/Odd Function Check: \(f(x)\) is symmetrical about the y-axis, hence it is an even function. For even functions, all sine terms vanish (\(b_n = 0\)).

4. Solution Method:

  • Verify \(b_n = 0\) to instantly eliminate options containing sine terms.
  • Calculate the DC component / constant term \(a_0 / 2\).
  • Calculate the general cosine coefficient \(a_n\) and expand for \(n = 1, 2, 3...\) to match the correct option.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Determine \(a_0\):
    \[a_0 = \dfrac{1}{L} \int_{-L}^{L} f(x) dx = \dfrac{2}{L} \int_{0}^{L} f(x) dx \]
    \[ a_0 = \dfrac{2}{2} \int_{0}^{1} 2k \, dx + \int_{1}^{2} 0 \, dx = [2kx]_0^1 = 2k \]
    Therefore, the constant term in the series \(\dfrac{a_0}{2} = \dfrac{2k}{2} = k\). (This eliminates Option A).
  2. Determine \(a_n\):
    \[a_n = \dfrac{2}{L} \int_{0}^{L} f(x) \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{L}\right) dx = \dfrac{2}{2} \int_{0}^{1} 2k \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{2}\right) dx \]
    \[ a_n = 2k \left[\dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{2}\right)}{\dfrac{n\pi}{2}} \right]_0^1 = \dfrac{4k}{n\pi} \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi}{2}\right) \]
  3. Evaluate \(a_n\) for different values of \(n\):
    For \(n=1\): \(a_1 = \dfrac{4k}{\pi} \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \dfrac{4k}{\pi}\)
    For \(n=2\): \(a_2 = \dfrac{4k}{2\pi} \sin(\pi) = 0\)
    For \(n=3\): \(a_3 = \dfrac{4k}{3\pi} \sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) = -\dfrac{4k}{3\pi}\)
    For \(n=4\): \(a_4 = 0\)
    For \(n=5\): \(a_5 = \dfrac{4k}{5\pi} \sin\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{2}\right) = \dfrac{4k}{5\pi}\)
  4. Construct the final Fourier series:
    \[f(x) = k + \dfrac{4k}{\pi} \left( \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}x\right) - \dfrac{1}{3}\cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}x\right) + \dfrac{1}{5}\cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{2}x\right) - \dots \right) \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(f(x)=k+\dfrac{4k}{\pi}(cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}x-\dfrac{1}{3}cos\dfrac{3\pi}{2}x+\dfrac{1}{5}cos\dfrac{5\pi}{2}x-+\dots)\) | Option(s): C

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q14
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
X is a random variable that can take any one of the values 0, 1, 7, 11, and 12. The probability mass function for X is
\(P(X = 0) = 0.4\); \(P(X = 1) = 0.3\); \(P(X = 7) = 0.1\);
\(P(X = 11) = 0.1\); \(P(X = 12) = 0.1\)
Then, the variance of X is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability and Statistics / Random Variables

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: 3. Application
  • Given Data: Random Variable \(X \in \{0, 1, 7, 11, 12\}\)
    PMF: \(P(X=0)=0.4\); \(P(X=1)=0.3\); \(P(X=7)=0.1\); \(P(X=11)=0.1\); \(P(X=12)=0.1\)
  • Aim: Calculate the variance of \(X\).

3. Core Concepts:

Expected Value (Mean): \(E[X] = \sum x_i \cdot P(x_i)\)

Expected Value of Squares: \(E[X^2] = \sum x_i^2 \cdot P(x_i)\)

Variance Formula: \(\text{Var}(X) = E[X^2] - (E[X])^2\)

4. Solution Method:

  • Verify that the sum of probabilities is 1.0 (Sanity check: \(0.4+0.3+0.1+0.1+0.1 = 1.0\), OK).
  • Compute the expected value \(E[X]\).
  • Compute \(E[X^2]\).
  • Apply the variance formula.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Compute the Expected Value \(E[X]\):
    \[ E[X] = (0 \times 0.4) + (1 \times 0.3) + (7 \times 0.1) + (11 \times 0.1) + (12 \times 0.1) \]
    \[ E[X] = 0 + 0.3 + 0.7 + 1.1 + 1.2 = 3.3 \]
  2. Compute \(E[X^2]\):
    \[ E[X^2] = (0^2 \times 0.4) + (1^2 \times 0.3) + (7^2 \times 0.1) + (11^2 \times 0.1) + (12^2 \times 0.1) \]
    \[ E[X^2] = 0 + 0.3 + 4.9 + 12.1 + 14.4 = 31.7 \]
  3. Compute Variance \(\text{Var}(X)\):
    \[ \text{Var}(X) = E[X^2] - (E[X])^2 \]
    \[\text{Var}(X) = 31.7 - (3.3)^2 = 31.7 - 10.89 = 20.81 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 20.81 | Option(s): A

questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Partial Differential Equations (Order, Linearity, Homogeneity)

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    Four differential equations involving \(u\) and its partial derivatives (options A–D), with constant \(c\) and independent variables \(x,y,z,t\).
  • Aim: Identify which equation(s) are second-order, linear, and homogeneous partial differential equations.

Core Concepts

Theory:

  • Order: The highest order of partial derivative present in the equation.
  • Linearity: A PDE is linear if \(u\) and all its derivatives appear to the first power and are not multiplied together or inside nonlinear functions. Coefficients may depend on independent variables, but not on \(u\).
  • Homogeneity: A linear PDE is homogeneous if it can be written as \(L(u)=0\), i.e., there is no term independent of \(u\) (no forcing/source term like \(xy\), constants, etc.).

Canonical linear homogeneous form:
\[L(u) = 0 \]
where \(L\) is a linear differential operator (e.g., Laplacian, wave operator).

Standard assumptions: The classification is based purely on the mathematical structure (order, linearity, and presence/absence of forcing term), not on boundary/initial conditions.

Solution Method

  • Logic flow: For each option: (i) determine the highest derivative order \( ightarrow\) (ii) test linearity (no powers/products of derivatives) \( ightarrow\) (iii) test homogeneity (no standalone forcing term).
  • Alternatives: Rewrite each equation in operator form \(L(u)=f\). If \(f=0\), it is homogeneous; if \(f eq 0\), non-homogeneous.
  • Common pitfalls to avoid: (i) Calling an equation “homogeneous” just because \(u\) terms look similar on both sides; (ii) overlooking nonlinearities like \((u_{tt})^2\); (iii) confusing first-order PDE with second-order PDE.

Step-by-Step Execution

  1. Option (A):
    \(\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} = c^2\left(\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} + \dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2} ight) + xy\)
    Order: second (contains \(u_{tt}, u_{xx}, u_{yy}\)).
    Linearity: linear in \(u\) and its derivatives.
    Homogeneity test: presence of forcing term \(xy\) (independent of \(u\)) implies \(L(u)=xy eq 0\). Hence non-homogeneous. Reject.
  2. Option (B):
    \(\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}+\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2}+\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial z^2}=0\)
    Order: second (highest derivative is second).
    Linearity: each derivative appears to the first power; no products/nonlinear functions. So linear.
    Homogeneity: right-hand side is zero, i.e., \(L(u)=0\). So homogeneous. Accept.
  3. Option (C):
    \(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial t} = c\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x}\)
    Order: first (only first derivatives). Therefore it is not second-order. Reject.
  4. Option (D):
    \(\left(\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} ight)^2 = c^2\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}\)
    Order: second (contains second derivatives).
    Linearity test: term \(\left(u_{tt} ight)^2\) is a square of a derivative, hence the equation is nonlinear. Reject.
  5. Conclusion: Only option (B) satisfies all three conditions: second-order, linear, homogeneous.

Validation & Error Handling:
Sanity check: Option (B) is the classic 3D Laplace equation \( abla^2 u=0\), which is universally recognized as second-order, linear, homogeneous. All rejections are consistent with standard definitions (forcing term in A, order mismatch in C, nonlinearity in D).

Final Answer

Final Answer: Option(s): B

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q36
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The value of \( \lim_{x \to \infty} (x - \sqrt{x^2 + x}) \) is equal to
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus / Limits

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: The limit expression \(\lim_{x \to \infty}(x - \sqrt{x^2 + x})\).
  • Aim: Evaluate the limit as \(x\) approaches infinity.

Core Concepts:

Indeterminate Forms: Direct substitution of \(\infty\) yields the indeterminate form \(\infty - \infty\).

Rationalization: For algebraic limits involving square roots and \(\infty - \infty\) forms, multiply and divide by the conjugate \((x + \sqrt{x^2+x})\) to convert to a manageable form, then simplify.

Solution:

  1. Rationalize the expression by multiplying by the conjugate:
    \[L = \lim_{x \to \infty} \dfrac{(x - \sqrt{x^2+x})(x + \sqrt{x^2+x})}{x + \sqrt{x^2+x}} \]
  2. Apply difference of squares \((a-b)(a+b) = a^2 - b^2\):
    \[L = \lim_{x \to \infty} \dfrac{x^2 - (x^2 + x)}{x + \sqrt{x^2+x}} = \lim_{x \to \infty} \dfrac{-x}{x + \sqrt{x^2\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)}} \]
  3. Simplify — since \(x \to \infty\), \(x\) is positive so \(\sqrt{x^2} = x\):
    \[L = \lim_{x \to \infty} \dfrac{-x}{x + x\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{1}{x}}} \]
  4. Divide numerator and denominator by \(x\):
    \[L = \lim_{x \to \infty} \dfrac{-1}{1 + \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{1}{x}}} \]
  5. Evaluate as \(x \to \infty\) (noting \(\dfrac{1}{x} \to 0\)):
    \[L = \dfrac{-1}{1 + \sqrt{1+0}} = \dfrac{-1}{1+1} = -0.5 \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: −0.5 | Option: B

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q47
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: Let y be the solution of the initial value problem \( y'' + 0.8y' + 0.16y = 0 \), where \( y(0) = 3 \) and \( y'(0) = 4.5 \). Then, \( y(1) \) is equal to _______________ (rounded off to 1 decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Differential Equations

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    ODE: \(y'' + 0.8y' + 0.16y = 0\)
    Initial conditions: \(y(0) = 3\), \(y'(0) = 4.5\)
  • Aim: Evaluate \(y(1)\) rounded to 1 decimal place.

Core Concepts:

Second-order linear homogeneous ODE with constant coefficients. The nature of the roots of the characteristic equation determines the form of the general solution.

Solution:

  1. Characteristic Equation:
    \[r^2 + 0.8r + 0.16 = 0 \Rightarrow (r+0.4)^2 = 0 \]
    Roots are real and repeated: \(r = -0.4\).
  2. General Solution (repeated roots):
    \[y(t) = (C_1 + C_2 t)e^{-0.4t} \]
  3. Apply \(y(0) = 3\):
    \[3 = C_1 e^0 \Rightarrow C_1 = 3 \]
  4. Differentiate using product rule:
    \[y'(t) = C_2 e^{-0.4t} - 0.4(C_1 + C_2 t)e^{-0.4t} \]
  5. Apply \(y'(0) = 4.5\):
    \[4.5 = C_2 - 0.4(3) \Rightarrow C_2 = 4.5 + 1.2 = 5.7 \]
  6. Evaluate \(y(1)\):
    \[y(t) = (3 + 5.7t)e^{-0.4t} \]
    \[y(1) = (3 + 5.7) \times e^{-0.4} = 8.7 \times 0.67032 \approx 5.8317 \]
    Rounded to 1 decimal place: 5.8

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 5.8 | NAT Key Range: 5.7 to 5.9

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q48
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The maximum value of the function \( h(x) = -x^3 + 2x^2 \) in the interval [-1,1.5] is equal to _______________ (rounded off to 1 decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus / Maxima & Minima

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: \(h(x) = -x^3 + 2x^2\) on the closed interval \([-1,\ 1.5]\).
  • Aim: Find the maximum value of the function in the given interval, rounded to 1 decimal place.

Core Concepts:

Extreme Value Theorem: The absolute maximum of a continuous function on a closed interval occurs either at a critical point (where \(h'(x) = 0\)) or at one of the interval endpoints.

Solution:

  1. First Derivative:
    \[h'(x) = -3x^2 + 4x \]
  2. Critical Points (set \(h'(x) = 0\)):
    \[-x(3x-4) = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0 \text{ and } x = \dfrac{4}{3} \approx 1.333 \]
    Both lie within \([-1,\ 1.5]\).
  3. Evaluate \(h(x)\) at critical points and boundaries:
    \(x\)\(h(x)\)
    \(-1\) (boundary)\(-(-1)^3 + 2(-1)^2 = 1 + 2 = \mathbf{3}\)
    \(0\) (critical)\(0\)
    \(4/3\) (critical)\(-\dfrac{64}{27} + \dfrac{96}{27} = \dfrac{32}{27} \approx 1.185\)
    \(1.5\) (boundary)\(-3.375 + 4.5 = 1.125\)
  4. Global Maximum: Comparing all values (3, 0, 1.185, 1.125), the maximum occurs at \(x = -1\) with \(h(-1) = 3.0\).

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 3.0 | NAT Key Range: 2.9 to 3.1

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Consider the differential equation given below. Using the Euler method with the step size (h) of 0.5, the value of y at x = 1.0 is equal to _______________ (rounded off to 1 decimal place).

\( \dfrac{dy}{dx} = y + 2x - x^2; \quad y(0) = 1 \quad (0 \le x < \infty) \)
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Differential Equations / Euler Method

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    ODE: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y + 2x - x^2\)
    Initial condition: \(y(0) = 1\)
    Step size: \(h = 0.5\)
  • Aim: Find \(y\) at \(x = 1.0\) using the Euler method, rounded to 1 decimal place.

Core Concepts:

The Euler method is a first-order numerical procedure for solving ODEs with a given initial value.

\[y_{n+1} = y_n + h \cdot f(x_n, y_n) \]

Solution:

  1. Initialization: \(x_0 = 0\), \(y_0 = 1\), \(f(x,y) = y + 2x - x^2\)
  2. Step 1 — Find \(y_1\) at \(x_1 = 0.5\):
    Evaluate slope: \(f(0,1) = 1 + 2(0) - (0)^2 = 1\)
    \[y_1 = 1 + 0.5 \times 1 = 1.5 \]
  3. Step 2 — Find \(y_2\) at \(x_2 = 1.0\):
    Evaluate slope at \((0.5,\ 1.5)\):
    \[f(0.5,\ 1.5) = 1.5 + 2(0.5) - (0.5)^2 = 1.5 + 1.0 - 0.25 = 2.25 \]
    \[y_2 = 1.5 + 0.5 \times 2.25 = 1.5 + 1.125 = 2.625 \]
  4. Rounded to 1 decimal place: 2.6

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2.6 | Range: 2.4 to 2.8

questions.question:
For the matrix \([A]\) given below, the transpose is _______.
\[[A] = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 4 & 5 \\ 4 & 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\]
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Matrix Algebra (Transpose)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data: 3×3 square matrix [A] with elements: Row 1 = [2, 3, 4], Row 2 = [1, 4, 5], Row 3 = [4, 3, 2].
  • Aim: Identify the transpose matrix from the four options.

Core Concepts:

Transpose operation: \([A]^T = [A_{ji}]\) where every element \(a_{ij}\) of the original becomes \(a_{ji}\). Rows of \([A]\) become columns of \([A]^T\) (and vice-versa). Property: \(([A]^T)^T = [A]\).

Common pitfalls: Mixing with adjoint (cofactors) or inverse.

Solution:

  1. Column 1 of [A] → Row 1 of \([A]^T\) → [2, 1, 4]
  2. Column 2 of [A] → Row 2 of \([A]^T\) → [3, 4, 3]
  3. Column 3 of [A] → Row 3 of \([A]^T\) → [4, 5, 2]
  4. Resulting transpose matrix:
    \[[A]^T = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\]
  5. Exact match with option (A).

Final Answer:

\(\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\) | Option(s): A

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q12
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Integration of \( ln(x) \) with x i.e.,
\( \displaystyle \int ln(x) dx = \) ______.
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Integral Calculus (Indefinite Integration)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data: Integrand \(= \ln(x)\) (natural logarithm, \(x > 0\)).
  • Aim: Evaluate indefinite integral \(\int \ln(x)\, dx\) and match with the correct option.

Core Concepts:

Integration by Parts Formula: \(\int u\, dv = uv - \int v\, du\)

Choose \(u = \ln(x)\) (easy to differentiate) and \(dv = dx\) (easy to integrate).

Common pitfalls: Forgetting the \(-x\) term or sign error in parts.

Solution:

  1. Let \(u = \ln(x) \Rightarrow du = \dfrac{1}{x}\, dx\)
  2. \(dv = dx \Rightarrow v = x\)
  3. Apply integration by parts:
    \[\int \ln(x)\, dx = x\ln(x) - \int x \cdot \dfrac{1}{x}\, dx\]
  4. Simplify the remaining integral:
    \[= x\ln(x) - \int 1\, dx = x\ln(x) - x + C\]
  5. Verification by differentiation:
    \[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[x\ln(x) - x\right] = \ln(x) + x \cdot \dfrac{1}{x} - 1 = \ln(x) \quad \checkmark\]

Final Answer:

\(x\ln(x) - x + C\) | Option(s): A

questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Vector Calculus in Fluid Kinematics (2-D Flow Field)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension + Application
  • Given Data: 2-D velocity vector \(\vec{V} = u\,\hat{x} + v\,\hat{y}\) (no z-component, i.e., \(w = 0\)).
  • Aim: Identify correct expressions for the z-component of curl and divergence.

Core Concepts:

Curl in Cartesian coordinates:

\[\nabla \times \vec{V} = \left(\dfrac{\partial w}{\partial y} - \dfrac{\partial v}{\partial z}\right)\hat{x} + \left(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial z} - \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial x}\right)\hat{y} + \left(\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial x} - \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y}\right)\hat{z}\]

For 2-D flow (\(w=0\), \(\partial/\partial z = 0\)), the z-component simplifies to \(\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial x} - \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y}\).

Divergence (continuity for incompressible flow):

\[\nabla \cdot \vec{V} = \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x} + \dfrac{\partial v}{\partial y} + \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial z}\]

Reduces to \(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x} + \dfrac{\partial v}{\partial y}\) for 2-D flow.

Common pitfall: Confusing the sign in curl (remember the right-hand rule).

Solution:

  1. z-component of curl: Substitute \(w=0\) → \(\left(\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial x} - \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial y}\right)\hat{z}\) → matches option (A). Option (B) has reversed sign → incorrect.
  2. Divergence: \(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x} + \dfrac{\partial v}{\partial y}\) → matches option (C). Option (D) uses cross derivatives → incorrect.

Final Answer:

Options A and C | Option(s): A; C

Probability & Statistics | Basic Probability Axioms & Conditional Probability

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension + Application
  • Given Data: A and B are non-null (non-empty) events.
  • Aim: Identify correct probability statements.

Core Concepts:

  • Mutually exclusive: \(A \cap B = \emptyset \Rightarrow P(A \cap B) = 0\), \(P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B)\).
  • Independent: \(P(A \cap B) = P(A)\cdot P(B)\).
  • Conditional probability: \(P(A|B) = \dfrac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}\). If \(B \subset A\), then \(A \cap B = B \Rightarrow P(A|B) = 1\).

Common pitfall: Mixing mutually exclusive with independent events.

Solution:

  1. Option (A): Mutually exclusive ⇒ \(P(A \cap B) = 0 \neq P(A)\cdot P(B)\) in general → incorrect.
  2. Option (B): \(B \subset A \Rightarrow P(A|B) = 1\) → correct.
  3. Option (C): Mutually exclusive ⇒ \(P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B)\) → correct.
  4. Option (D): Independent ⇒ \(P(A \cap B) = P(A)\cdot P(B) \neq 0\) in general → incorrect.

Final Answer:

Options B and C | Option(s): B; C

The “order” of the following ordinary differential equation is _______.
\[\dfrac{d^3y}{dx^3} + \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^6 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^4 + y = 0 \]
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Ordinary Differential Equations

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: ODE: \(\dfrac{d^3 y}{dx^3} + \left(\dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2}\right)^6 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^4 + y = 0\)
  • Aim: Find the order of the ODE.

Core Concepts:

Order of a differential equation = the highest order of derivative appearing in the equation. Powers or exponents applied to lower-order derivative terms do not affect the order.

Solution:

  1. Identify all derivative terms present: third derivative \(\left(\dfrac{d^3 y}{dx^3}\right)\), second derivative raised to power 6, first derivative raised to power 4, and zero-order term \(y\).
  2. Highest derivative present = third order.
  3. Therefore, Order = 3.

Final Answer:

3 | Option(s): 3

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q36

questions.question:
Pick the CORRECT solution for the following differential equation
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{x-y} \]
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Differential Equations

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{x-y}\).
  • Aim: Identify the correct general solution.

Core Concepts:

Separation of Variables: A first-order ODE of the form \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = f(x)\,g(y)\) is solved by rearranging so that all \(y\) terms are on one side and all \(x\) terms on the other.

Exponent Law: \(e^{a-b} = \dfrac{e^a}{e^b}\).

Solution:

  1. Rewrite the equation using exponent laws:
    \[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^x \cdot e^{-y} = \dfrac{e^x}{e^y}\]
  2. Separate variables — multiply both sides by \(e^y\,dx\):
    \[e^y\,dy = e^x\,dx\]
  3. Integrate both sides:
    \[\int e^y\,dy = \int e^x\,dx\]\[e^y = e^x + C\]
  4. Isolate \(y\) by taking the natural logarithm of both sides:
    \[y = \ln(e^x + C)\]where \(C\) is the constant of integration.

Final Answer:

\(y = \ln(e^x + C)\) | Option(s): A

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: \(f(x) = x^3 - \dfrac{15}{2}x^2 + 18x + 20\)
  • Aim: Identify correct statements regarding local maxima and minima (MSQ).

Core Concepts:

  • Critical Points: Found by setting \(f'(x) = 0\).
  • Second Derivative Test: If \(f''(x) > 0\) at a critical point → local minimum; if \(f''(x) < 0\) → local maximum.

Solution:

  1. First derivative:
    \[f'(x) = 3x^2 - 15x + 18\]
  2. Find critical points (set \(f'(x) = 0\)):
    \[3(x^2 - 5x + 6) = 0 \Rightarrow (x-2)(x-3) = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2,\; x = 3\]
  3. Second derivative: \(f''(x) = 6x - 15\)
  4. Evaluate at \(x = 2\): \(f''(2) = 12 - 15 = -3 < 0\) → local maximum at \(x = 2\). (Matches Option D)
  5. Evaluate at \(x = 3\): \(f''(3) = 18 - 15 = 3 > 0\) → local minimum at \(x = 3\). (Matches Option A)

Final Answer:

Statements A and D are correct | Option(s): A, D

questions.question:
Pick the CORRECT eigen value(s) of the matrix [A] from the following choices.
\[[A] = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 8 \\ 4 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\]
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra — Eigenvalues

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: \([A] = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 8 \\ 4 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\)
  • Aim: Identify the correct eigenvalue(s) from the given choices (MSQ).

Core Concepts:

  • Trace Property: \(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2 = \text{tr}(A) = a_{11} + a_{22}\)
  • Determinant Property: \(\lambda_1 \times \lambda_2 = |A|\)
  • Characteristic Equation for a \(2 \times 2\) matrix: \(\lambda^2 - (\text{Trace})\lambda + \text{Determinant} = 0\)

Solution:

  1. Trace: \(6 + 2 = 8\)
  2. Determinant: \((6 \times 2) - (8 \times 4) = 12 - 32 = -20\)
  3. Characteristic equation:
    \[\lambda^2 - 8\lambda - 20 = 0\]
  4. Factorise:
    \[(\lambda - 10)(\lambda + 2) = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda_1 = 10,\quad \lambda_2 = -2\]
  5. Verification: \(10 + (-2) = 8\) ✓ (equals Trace); \(10 \times (-2) = -20\) ✓ (equals Determinant).

Final Answer:

Eigenvalues are 10 and −2 | Option(s): A, C

questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability and Statistics

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Discrete random variable \(X\) with values \(x_i\): 1, 2, 4, 8 and corresponding probabilities \(P(X=x_i)\): 0.3, 0.1, 0.3, 0.3.
  • Aim: Calculate the standard deviation, rounded to one decimal place.

Core Concepts:

  • Mean: \(\mu = E[X] = \sum(x_i \cdot P(x_i))\)
  • Variance: \(\sigma^2 = E[X^2] - (E[X])^2\)
  • Standard Deviation: \(\sigma = \sqrt{\sigma^2}\)

Solution:

  1. Verify probability sum: \(0.3 + 0.1 + 0.3 + 0.3 = 1.0\) ✓
  2. Calculate \(E[X]\):
    \[E[X] = (1 \times 0.3) + (2 \times 0.1) + (4 \times 0.3) + (8 \times 0.3) = 0.3 + 0.2 + 1.2 + 2.4 = 4.1\]
  3. Calculate \(E[X^2]\):
    \[E[X^2] = (1^2 \times 0.3) + (2^2 \times 0.1) + (4^2 \times 0.3) + (8^2 \times 0.3)\]\[= 0.3 + 0.4 + 4.8 + 19.2 = 24.7\]
  4. Calculate Variance:
    \[\sigma^2 = E[X^2] - (E[X])^2 = 24.7 - (4.1)^2 = 24.7 - 16.81 = 7.89\]
  5. Calculate Standard Deviation:
    \[\sigma = \sqrt{7.89} = 2.809 \approx \mathbf{2.8}\]

Final Answer:

2.8 | Option(s): Range 2.7 to 2.9

The smallest positive root of the equation
\[x^5 - 5x^4 - 10x^3 + 50x^2 + 9x - 45 = 0 \]
lies in the range
questions.explanation:
Mathematics | Polynomial Equations / Roots of Equation

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Polynomial equation \(x^5 - 5x^4 - 10x^3 + 50x^2 + 9x - 45 = 0\)
  • Aim: Find the range containing the smallest positive root.

Core Concepts:

Rational Root Theorem: Possible rational roots = ±(factors of constant term) / (leading coefficient). For real roots, sign changes in \(f(x)\) or numerical verification are used to isolate roots.

Common Pitfall: Missing multiple roots or performing sign change analysis without testing candidate values.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. List possible rational roots: \(\pm 1, \pm 3, \pm 5, \pm 9, \pm 15, \pm 45\)

  2. Test \(x = 1\):\[1 - 5 - 10 + 50 + 9 - 45 = 0 \checkmark\]So \((x - 1)\) is a factor.

  3. Find all roots via synthetic division / factorisation:
    Roots = \(1,\; 3,\; 5,\; -1,\; -3\)

  4. Positive roots: 1, 3, 5
    Smallest positive root = 1 → lies in \(0 < x \leq 2\)

Final Answer:

Final Answer: Smallest positive root = 1, in range \(0 < x \leq 2\) | Option(s): A

questions.question:
The second-order differential equation in an unknown function \( u: u(x,y) \) is defined as

\[\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} = 2 \]

Assuming \( g: g(x), f: f(y) \), and \( h: h(y) \), the general solution of the above differential equation is
questions.explanation:
Mathematics | Partial Differential Equations / General Solution of PDE

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: \(\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} = 2\); \(u = u(x, y)\); arbitrary functions \(f(y)\) and \(h(y)\).
  • Aim: Find the general solution.

Core Concepts:

For a second-order PDE depending only on \(x\), integrate twice with respect to \(x\) treating \(y\) as a constant. An arbitrary function of \(y\) appears as the constant of integration after each step.

Common Pitfall: Forgetting the arbitrary function of \(y\) after the first integration step.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Integrate once w.r.t. \(x\):\[\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial x} = 2x + f(y)\]

  2. Integrate again w.r.t. \(x\):\[u = x^2 + x\cdot f(y) + h(y)\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(u = x^2 + x\,f(y) + h(y)\) | Option(s): B

questions.question: The probability that a student passes only in Mathematics is \( \dfrac{1}{3} \). The probability that the student passes only in English is \( \dfrac{4}{9} \). The probability that the student passes in both of these subjects is \( \dfrac{1}{6} \). The probability that the student will pass in at least one of these two subjects is
questions.explanation:
Mathematics | Probability / Addition Theorem of Probability

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • \(P(\text{only Math}) = \dfrac{1}{3}\)
    • \(P(\text{only English}) = \dfrac{4}{9}\)
    • \(P(\text{both}) = \dfrac{1}{6}\)
  • Aim: Find \(P(\text{at least one})\).

Core Concepts:

\[P(A \cup B) = P(\text{only } A) + P(\text{only } B) + P(A \cap B)\]The three regions (only A, only B, both) are mutually exclusive and their union covers "at least one".

Common Pitfall: Adding only \(P(\text{only})\) terms without including the intersection, or attempting \(1 - P(\text{neither})\) without correct data.

Step-by-Step Execution:

\[P(\text{at least one}) = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{4}{9} + \dfrac{1}{6}\]

Converting to common denominator 18:

\[= \dfrac{6}{18} + \dfrac{8}{18} + \dfrac{3}{18} = \dfrac{17}{18}\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{17}{18}\) | Option(s): A

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q28
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
For the following partial differential equation,
\[x \dfrac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2} + y \dfrac{\partial^2 f}{\partial y^2} = \dfrac{x^2 + y^2}{2} \]
which of the following option(s) is/are CORRECT?
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Partial Differential Equations / Classification of Second-Order PDEs

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: PDE: \(x\dfrac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2} + y\dfrac{\partial^2 f}{\partial y^2} = \dfrac{x^2+y^2}{2}\); regions specified in options (\(x>0, y>0\); \(x=0, y>0\); \(x<0, y>0\)).
  • Aim: Determine the type of PDE (elliptic, parabolic, hyperbolic) in the specified regions.

Core Concepts:

Second-order linear PDEs are classified based on the discriminant of the principal part (highest-order derivatives), analogous to conic sections.

General form: \(A\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} + 2H\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x\partial y} + B\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2} + \text{lower order terms} = G\)

Discriminant: \(D = H^2 - AB\)
\(D < 0\) → Elliptic  |  \(D = 0\) → Parabolic  |  \(D > 0\) → Hyperbolic

Classification is independent of lower-order terms and the RHS. It holds pointwise in the domain.

Common Pitfalls: Ignoring that classification depends on the signs of \(x\) and \(y\); mistakenly assuming the RHS affects type; assuming uniform type across all regions.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify coefficients from \(x f_{xx} + y f_{yy} = \dfrac{x^2+y^2}{2}\) (no mixed derivative term):
    \(A = x\),   \(H = 0\),   \(B = y\)

  2. Compute discriminant:\[D = H^2 - AB = 0 - (x)(y) = -xy\]

  3. Region \(x > 0,\; y > 0\): \(xy > 0 \implies D = -xy < 0\) → Elliptic ✓ (Option A correct)

  4. Region \(x > 0,\; y > 0\): \(D < 0 \neq 0\) → Not parabolic (Option B incorrect)

  5. Region \(x = 0,\; y > 0\): \(A = 0\), PDE reduces to \(yf_{yy} = \dfrac{y^2}{2}\), which is an ODE in \(y\) only → not classifiable as a 2D PDE type (Option C incorrect)

  6. Region \(x < 0,\; y > 0\): \(xy < 0 \implies D = -xy > 0\) → Hyperbolic ✓ (Option D correct)

Final Answer:

Final Answer: A and D are correct | Option(s): A, D

The value of \( f(1.5) \) estimated using second-order Newton’s interpolation formula is __________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods / Interpolation

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • \(x_0 = 1,\; f(x_0) = 0\)
    • \(x_1 = 2,\; f(x_1) = 0.3010\)
    • \(x_2 = 3,\; f(x_2) = 0.4771\)
    • Evaluation point \(x = 1.5\)
  • Aim: Estimate \(f(1.5)\) using second-order Newton's interpolation formula, rounded to 2 decimal places.

Core Concepts:

Newton's Divided Difference Formula (second-order):\[f(x) \approx f(x_0) + f[x_0,x_1](x-x_0) + f[x_0,x_1,x_2](x-x_0)(x-x_1)\]

First divided difference: \(f[x_i, x_{i+1}] = \dfrac{f(x_{i+1}) - f(x_i)}{x_{i+1} - x_i}\)

Second divided difference: \(f[x_0,x_1,x_2] = \dfrac{f[x_1,x_2] - f[x_0,x_1]}{x_2 - x_0}\)

Common Pitfall: Rounding intermediate values too early; using finite differences without dividing by \(h^k\) for divided differences.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. First divided differences:\[f[x_0, x_1] = \dfrac{0.3010 - 0}{2 - 1} = 0.3010\]\[f[x_1, x_2] = \dfrac{0.4771 - 0.3010}{3 - 2} = 0.1761\]

  2. Second divided difference:\[f[x_0, x_1, x_2] = \dfrac{0.1761 - 0.3010}{3 - 1} = \dfrac{-0.1249}{2} = -0.06245\]

  3. Apply Newton's formula at \(x = 1.5\):\[f(1.5) = 0 + 0.3010(1.5-1) + (-0.06245)(1.5-1)(1.5-2)\]

  4. Evaluate each term:
    First term: \(0.3010 \times 0.5 = 0.1505\)
    Second term: \((-0.06245) \times (0.5) \times (-0.5) = (-0.06245)\times(-0.25) = 0.015613\)
    \[f(1.5) = 0.1505 + 0.015613 = 0.166113\]

  5. Round to 2 decimal places: 0.17
    Sanity check: Actual \(\log_{10}(1.5) \approx 0.176\); higher-order terms would improve precision.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.17

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q36
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: What are the eigenvalues of the matrix \( \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \)?
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra / Eigenvalues

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data: Matrix \(A = egin{bmatrix}2&1&1\ 1&4&1\ 1&1&2\end{bmatrix}\)
  • Aim: Find the eigenvalues of the matrix.

Core Concepts:

Trace Property: The sum of the eigenvalues of a matrix is equal to its trace (the sum of the main diagonal elements).\[\sum \lambda_i = ext{Tr}(A)\]

Determinant Property: The product of the eigenvalues of a matrix is equal to its determinant.\[\prod \lambda_i = |A|\]

Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the trace of matrix \(A\).
  2. Calculate the determinant of matrix \(A\).
  3. Check the given options to see which set of eigenvalues satisfies both the trace and determinant conditions. Using matrix properties is a much more efficient strategy for competitive exams than solving the cubic characteristic equation \(|A - \lambda I| = 0\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Calculate the Trace of A:

\[ ext{Tr}(A) = 2 + 4 + 2 = 8\]

The sum of the eigenvalues must be 8. Evaluating the given options:

  • (A) \(1 + 2 + 5 = 8\) ✓
  • (B) \(1 + 3 + 4 = 8\) ✓
  • (C) \(-5 + 1 + 2 = -2 eq 8\) ✗ — Eliminated
  • (D) \(-5 - 1 + 2 = -4 eq 8\) ✗ — Eliminated

Step 2: Calculate the Determinant of A:

\[|A| = 2(4 imes 2 - 1 imes 1) - 1(1 imes 2 - 1 imes 1) + 1(1 imes 1 - 4 imes 1)\]\[|A| = 2(8 - 1) - 1(2 - 1) + 1(1 - 4)\]\[|A| = 2(7) - 1(1) + 1(-3) = 14 - 1 - 3 = 10\]

The product of the eigenvalues must be 10. Checking remaining options:

  • (A) \(1 imes 2 imes 5 = 10\) ✓
  • (B) \(1 imes 3 imes 4 = 12 eq 10\) ✗ — Eliminated

Only option (A) satisfies both the trace and determinant conditions.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1, 2, 5 | Option(s): A

questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Vector Calculus / Vector Identities

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given Data: A vector field \(\vec{p}\) and a scalar field \(r\) defined by polynomial equations. Statements evaluating null vector and zero field properties.
  • Aim: Determine the validity of statements P and Q regarding standard operations on \(\vec{p}\) and \(r\).
  • Note: Based on standard GATE vector calculus questions and the official key confirming both are TRUE, the question tests the universal vector identities: "P: The curl of the gradient of scalar field \(r\) is a null vector" and "Q: The divergence of the curl of vector field \(\vec{p}\) is zero."

Core Concepts:

Identity 1 — Curl of a Gradient: For any continuously twice-differentiable scalar field \(f\), the curl of its gradient is a null vector.\[ abla imes ( abla f) = \vec{0}\]

Identity 2 — Divergence of a Curl: For any continuously twice-differentiable vector field \(\vec{V}\), the divergence of its curl is identically zero.\[ abla \cdot ( abla imes \vec{V}) = 0\]

Solution Method:

Calculating the actual gradient, curl, and divergence for the provided complex polynomials is an intentional time-sink designed to distract test-takers. Recognizing standard vector calculus identities is the key to solving this instantly without computation.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Analyze Statement P: The gradient of a scalar field \(r\) (i.e., \( abla r\)) generates a conservative vector field. The curl of any conservative vector field is zero. Thus, \( abla imes ( abla r) = \vec{0}\). Statement P is TRUE.
  2. Analyze Statement Q: The curl of a vector field \(\vec{p}\) (i.e., \( abla imes \vec{p}\)) generates a solenoidal vector field. The divergence of any solenoidal vector field is zero. Thus, \( abla \cdot ( abla imes \vec{p}) = 0\). Statement Q is TRUE.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: Both P and Q are TRUE | Option(s): D

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 2 | CE Q11
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
A partial differential equation

\[\dfrac{\partial^2 T}{\partial x^2} + \dfrac{\partial^2 T}{\partial y^2} = 0 \]

is defined for the two-dimensional field \( T: T(x, y) \), inside a planar square domain of size 2 m × 2 m. Three boundary edges of the square domain are maintained at value \( T = 50 \), whereas the fourth boundary edge is maintained at \( T = 100 \).

The value of \( T \) at the center of the domain is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Partial Differential Equations (Laplace Equation – Dirichlet Problem)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Square domain of size \(2\text{ m} \times 2\text{ m}\); governing PDE \(\dfrac{\partial^2 T}{\partial x^2} + \dfrac{\partial^2 T}{\partial y^2} = 0\); three boundary edges at \(T = 50\); fourth boundary edge at \(T = 100\).
  • Aim: Evaluate \(T\) at the geometric centre of the domain.

Core Concepts:

Laplace's equation \(\nabla^2 T = 0\) admits harmonic solutions. The mean-value property of harmonic functions combined with linearity and the uniqueness theorem for the Dirichlet problem on a square imply that the centre value is exactly the arithmetic average of the four constant boundary temperatures — each side contributes equally by symmetry.

Superposition principle: \(T = 50 + u\), where \(u = 0\) on three sides and \(u = 50\) on the fourth. At the centre, \(u_c = 50/4 = 12.5\), hence \(T_c = 62.5\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. List boundary temperatures: 50, 50, 50, 100.
  2. Each side contributes \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) of its value at the centre (by symmetry).
    \[T_{\text{center}} = \dfrac{50 + 50 + 50 + 100}{4} = \dfrac{250}{4} = 62.5 \]
  3. Verify via superposition:
    \[T = 50 + u \implies u_{\text{center}} = \dfrac{50}{4} = 12.5 \implies T_{\text{center}} = 50 + 12.5 = 62.5 \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 62.5 | Correct option: (B)

questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrix Transpose Properties)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data: Matrices \(A\) and \(B\) are conformable for addition and multiplication.
    Statement P: \((A + B)^T = A^T + B^T\)
    Statement Q: \((AB)^T = A^T B^T\)
  • Aim: Identify which statement(s) is/are TRUE.

Core Concepts:

Standard transpose theorems: the sum rule \((A+B)^T = A^T + B^T\) always holds, while the product rule reverses order: \((AB)^T = B^T A^T\) (not \(A^T B^T\) as stated in Q).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. For P — element-wise verification:
    \[ [(A+B)^T]_{ij} = (A+B)_{ji} = A_{ji} + B_{ji} = (A^T)_{ij} + (B^T)_{ij} \]
    \(\therefore\) P is TRUE.
  2. For Q — element-wise verification:
    \[ [(AB)^T]_{ki} = (AB)_{ik} = \sum_j A_{ij} B_{jk} \]
    RHS of Q: \((A^T B^T)_{ki} = \sum_j A_{jk} B_{ij}\) — this does not equal the LHS.
    Correct identity: \((AB)^T = B^T A^T\)
    \(\therefore\) Q is FALSE.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: P is TRUE and Q is FALSE | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 2 | CE Q13
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
The second derivative of a function \( f \) is computed using the fourth-order Central Divided Difference method with a step length \( h \).

The CORRECT expression for the second derivative is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods | Finite-Difference Approximations

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Fourth-order central divided-difference scheme with uniform step length \(h\); function values \(f_{i+2},\, f_{i+1},\, f_i,\, f_{i-1},\, f_{i-2}\).
  • Aim: Identify the correct expression for the second derivative \(f''(x_i)\).

Core Concepts:

Taylor series expansion about \(x_i\) up to \(O(h^5)\) terms, followed by algebraic elimination of odd-powered terms, yields the fourth-order accurate central formula for \(f''\). Truncation error is \(O(h^4)\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Taylor Expansions:
    \[f_{i\pm1} = f_i \pm h f'_i + \dfrac{h^2}{2}f''_i \pm \dfrac{h^3}{6}f'''_i + \dfrac{h^4}{24}f^{(4)}_i + O(h^5) \]\[f_{i\pm2} = f_i \pm 2hf'_i + 2h^2 f''_i \pm \dfrac{4h^3}{3}f'''_i + \dfrac{2h^4}{3}f^{(4)}_i + O(h^5) \]
  2. Form linear combination to cancel \(f'\) and \(f'''\) terms:
    \(-f_{i+2} + 16f_{i+1} - 30f_i + 16f_{i-1} - f_{i-2}\)
  3. Divide by \(12h^2\):
    \[f''_i = \dfrac{-f_{i+2} + 16f_{i+1} - 30f_i + 16f_{i-1} - f_{i-2}}{12h^2} + O(h^4) \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{1}{12h^2}\left[-f_{i+2} + 16f_{i+1} - 30f_i + 16f_{i-1} - f_{i-2}\right]\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.question: The function \( f(x) = x^3 - 27x + 4 \), \( 1 \le x \le 6 \) has
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus | Applications of Derivatives (Maxima–Minima)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: \(f(x) = x^3 - 27x + 4\), closed interval \(1 \leq x \leq 6\).
  • Aim: Classify the nature of stationary point(s) inside the domain.

Core Concepts:

First-derivative test locates critical points; sign of \(f''(x)\) distinguishes maxima (\(f'' < 0\)) from minima (\(f'' > 0\)). An inflection requires \(f'' = 0\) with a concavity change; a saddle point applies only in multivariable calculus.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. First derivative:
    \[f'(x) = 3x^2 - 27 = 3(x^2 - 9) \]
    Set \(f'(x) = 0\): \(x = \pm 3\). Only \(x = 3\) lies in \([1, 6]\).
  2. Second derivative:
    \[f''(x) = 6x \implies f''(3) = 18 > 0 \]
    Concave up \(\rightarrow\) local minimum at \(x = 3\).
  3. \(x = -3\) is outside the domain. \(f''(x) = 0\) occurs at \(x = 0\) (also outside domain). No saddle point (single-variable function).

Final Answer:

Final Answer: Minima point at \(x = 3\) | Correct option: (B)
