questions.question: A one-dimensional domain is discretized into \( N \) sub-domains of width \( \Delta x \) with node numbers \( i = 0, 1, 2, 3, ..., N \). If the time scale is discretized in steps of \( \Delta t \), the forward-time and centered-space finite difference approximation at \( i^{th} \) node and \( n^{th} \) time step, for the partial differential equation \( \dfrac{\partial v}{\partial t} = \beta \dfrac{\partial^2 v}{\partial x^2} \) is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data: The 1-D partial differential equation (PDE): \(\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial t} = \beta \dfrac{\partial^2 v}{\partial x^2}\)
  • Aim: To construct the finite difference approximation using a forward-time and centered-space (FTCS) scheme at node \(i\) and time step \(n\).

3. Core Concepts:

Forward-Time Difference (First Order):

\[\dfrac{\partial v}{\partial t} \approx \dfrac{v_i^{(n+1)} - v_i^{(n)}}{\Delta t} \]

Centered-Space Difference (Second Order):

\[\dfrac{\partial^2 v}{\partial x^2} \approx \dfrac{v_{i+1}^{(n)} - 2v_i^{(n)} + v_{i-1}^{(n)}}{(\Delta x)^2} \]

4. Solution Method & Execution:

Substituting these standard finite difference approximations directly into the governing PDE:

\[ \dfrac{v_i^{(n+1)} - v_i^{(n)}}{\Delta t} = \beta \left[\dfrac{v_{i+1}^{(n)} - 2v_i^{(n)} + v_{i-1}^{(n)}}{(\Delta x)^2} \right] \]

This matches the formulation provided in Option (A).

Note: Option C utilizes backward-time, Option D utilizes centered-time, and Option B is structurally invalid.

5. Final Answer:

The valid FTCS scheme formula. | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q30
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: Consider two functions: \( x = \psi \ln \phi \) and \( y = \phi \ln \psi \). Which one of the following is the correct expression for \( \dfrac{\partial \psi}{\partial x} \)?
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Two coupled implicit functions: \(x = \psi \ln \phi\) and \(y = \phi \ln \psi\)
  • Aim: Extract the partial derivative \(\dfrac{\partial \psi}{\partial x}\).

3. Core Concepts:

To find \(\dfrac{\partial \psi}{\partial x}\), we treat \(x\) as the independent variable and look for how \(\psi\) changes, while keeping \(y\) strictly constant (which means \(dy = 0\)). We utilize the concept of implicit differentiation via total differentials.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Take the total differential of both equations:
    \[dx = (\ln \phi)\, d\psi + \left( \psi \cdot \dfrac{1}{\phi} \right) d\phi \quad \cdots \text{(Eq. 1)} \]\[dy = (\ln \psi)\, d\phi + \left( \phi \cdot \dfrac{1}{\psi} \right) d\psi \quad \cdots \text{(Eq. 2)} \]
  2. Apply the partial derivative condition (\(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}\) holds \(y\) constant, so \(dy = 0\)) in Eq. 2:
    \[0 = (\ln \psi)\, d\phi + \left( \dfrac{\phi}{\psi} \right) d\psi \]
    Express \(d\phi\) in terms of \(d\psi\):
    \[d\phi = - \left( \dfrac{\phi}{\psi \ln \psi} \right) d\psi \]
  3. Substitute \(d\phi\) into Eq. 1:
    \[ dx = (\ln \phi)\, d\psi + \dfrac{\psi}{\phi} \left[- \left( \dfrac{\phi}{\psi \ln \psi} \right) d\psi \right] \]\[dx = \left( \ln \phi - \dfrac{1}{\ln \psi} \right) d\psi \]\[dx = \left( \dfrac{\ln \phi \ln \psi - 1}{\ln \psi} \right) d\psi \]
  4. Rearrange to isolate the required derivative:
    \[\dfrac{\partial \psi}{\partial x} = \dfrac{d\psi}{dx} = \dfrac{\ln \psi}{\ln \phi \ln \psi - 1} \]

5. Final Answer:

\(\dfrac{\partial \psi}{\partial x} = \dfrac{\ln \psi}{\ln \phi \ln \psi - 1}\) | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 1 | CE Q44
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: Consider the ordinary differential equation \( x^2 \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 2x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2y = 0 \). Given the values of y(1) = 0 and y(2) = 2, the value of y(3) (round off to 1 decimal place), is ________
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Differential Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Differential equation: \(x^2 \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 2x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2y = 0\)
    • Boundary conditions: \(y(1) = 0\) and \(y(2) = 2\)
  • Aim: Evaluate \(y(3)\) and round off to 1 decimal place.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Cauchy-Euler Equation: A linear homogeneous ODE with variable coefficients of the form \(ax^2y'' + bxy' + cy = 0\).
  • Solved by substituting \(y = x^m\), which transforms the equation into an auxiliary algebraic equation: \(am(m-1) + bm + c = 0\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Formulate the characteristic equation.
  2. Find the roots \(m_1\) and \(m_2\).
  3. Write the general solution: \(y(x) = C_1 x^{m_1} + C_2 x^{m_2}\).
  4. Use the boundary conditions to find the constants \(C_1\) and \(C_2\).
  5. Substitute \(x = 3\) into the specific solution.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Characteristic Equation:
    Substitute \(y = x^m\), \(y' = mx^{m-1}\), \(y'' = m(m-1)x^{m-2}\):\[m(m-1) - 2m + 2 = 0 \implies m^2 - 3m + 2 = 0 \]
  2. Find Roots:\[(m-1)(m-2) = 0 \implies m_1 = 1,\ m_2 = 2 \]
  3. General Solution:\[y(x) = C_1 x + C_2 x^2 \]
  4. Apply Boundary Conditions:
    At \(x=1,\ y=0\):\[0 = C_1 + C_2 \implies C_1 = -C_2 \quad \cdots\text{(Eq. 1)} \]At \(x=2,\ y=2\):\[2 = 2C_1 + 4C_2 \implies C_1 + 2C_2 = 1 \quad \cdots\text{(Eq. 2)} \]Substituting Eq. 1 into Eq. 2:\[-C_2 + 2C_2 = 1 \implies C_2 = 1,\ C_1 = -1 \]Specific solution: \(y(x) = x^2 - x\)
  5. Evaluate at \(x = 3\):\[y(3) = (3)^2 - 3 = 9 - 3 = 6 \]

6. Final Answer:

\(y(3) = 6.0\) | Accepted key range: 5.9 to 6.1

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q3
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
The following inequality is true for all \(x\) close to 0.

\[2 - \dfrac{x^2}{3} < \dfrac{x \sin x}{1 - \cos x} < 2\]

What is the value of \(\displaystyle \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{x \sin x}{1 - \cos x}\)?
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus (Limits)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: The inequality \(2 - \dfrac{x^2}{3} < \dfrac{x \sin x}{1 - \cos x} < 2\) valid for all \(x\) close to 0.
  • Aim: Evaluate the limit \(\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{x \sin x}{1 - \cos x}\).

3. Core Concepts:

Squeeze Theorem (Sandwich Theorem): If \(f(x) \leq g(x) \leq h(x)\) for all \(x\) in an open interval containing \(c\), and \(\displaystyle\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = \lim_{x \to c} h(x) = L\), then \(\displaystyle\lim_{x \to c} g(x) = L\).

Alternative (Taylor Series Expansion): Maclaurin series for \(\sin x \approx x - \dfrac{x^3}{3!}\) and \(\cos x \approx 1 - \dfrac{x^2}{2!}\).

Alternative (L'Hôpital's Rule): For \(0/0\) indeterminate forms, \(\displaystyle\lim \dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)} = \lim \dfrac{f'(x)}{g'(x)}\).

4. Solution Method:

The problem practically hands over the answer by providing the bounding functions. We will use the Squeeze Theorem for the primary solution, as it requires zero calculus operations. For deep clarity, the Taylor series approach is also demonstrated.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Method 1: Squeeze Theorem (Fastest)

  1. Step 1: Identify \(f(x)\) and \(h(x)\).\[f(x) = 2 - \dfrac{x^2}{3}, \quad h(x) = 2 \]
  2. Step 2: Evaluate the limits of the bounding functions as \(x \to 0\).\[\lim_{x \to 0} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 0} \left(2 - \dfrac{x^2}{3}\right) = 2 \]\[\lim_{x \to 0} h(x) = 2 \]
  3. Step 3: Apply the Squeeze Theorem. Since both boundaries approach 2, the function trapped between them must also approach 2.\[\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{x \sin x}{1 - \cos x} = 2 \]

Method 2: Taylor Series (Verification)

  1. Step 1: Substitute series approximations: \(\sin x \approx x\), \(\cos x \approx 1 - \dfrac{x^2}{2}\)
  2. Step 2: Evaluate the expression.\[\dfrac{x \cdot x}{1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{x^2}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{x^2}{x^2/2} = 2 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(2\) | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q4
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: What is curl of the vector field \(2x^2y\mathbf{i} + 5z^2\mathbf{j} - 4yz\mathbf{k}\) ?
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Vector Calculus

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Vector field \(\mathbf{V} = 2x^2y\,\mathbf{i} + 5z^2\,\mathbf{j} - 4yz\,\mathbf{k}\)
  • Aim: Find the curl of the vector field \(\mathbf{V}\).

3. Core Concepts:

Curl of a Vector Field: Represents the infinitesimal rotation (circulation) of a 3D vector field.

Formula: For a vector field \(\mathbf{V} = P\,\mathbf{i} + Q\,\mathbf{j} + R\,\mathbf{k}\), the curl is determined by the cross product of the del operator \(( abla)\) and the vector field:

\[ abla imes \mathbf{V} = egin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \ \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z} \ P & Q & R \end{vmatrix} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Construct the determinant matrix.
  2. Expand the determinant along the first row (\(\mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j}, \mathbf{k}\)).
  3. Compute the partial derivatives meticulously. Treat other variables as constants during partial differentiation.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Set up the determinant.\[ abla imes \mathbf{V} = egin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \ \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z} \ 2x^2y & 5z^2 & -4yz \end{vmatrix} \]
  2. Step 2: Expand the determinant.\[ = \mathbf{i} \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(-4yz) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(5z^2) ight] - \mathbf{j} \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(-4yz) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(2x^2y) ight] + \mathbf{k} \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(5z^2) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(2x^2y) ight] \]
  3. Step 3: Calculate the partial derivatives.
    • For \(\mathbf{i}\): \(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(-4yz) = -4z\), and \(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(5z^2) = 10z\)
    • For \(\mathbf{j}\): \(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(-4yz) = 0\), and \(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(2x^2y) = 0\)
    • For \(\mathbf{k}\): \(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(5z^2) = 0\), and \(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(2x^2y) = 2x^2\)
  4. Step 4: Substitute back and simplify.\[ = \mathbf{i}[(-4z) - (10z)] - \mathbf{j}[0 - 0] + \mathbf{k}[0 - (2x^2)] \]\[= -14z\,\mathbf{i} - 2x^2\,\mathbf{k} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(-14z\,\mathbf{i} - 2x^2\,\mathbf{k}\) | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q18
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The value of the function \(f(x)\) is given at \(n\) distinct values of \(x\) and its value is to be interpolated at the point \(x^*\), using all the \(n\) points. The estimate is obtained first by the Lagrange polynomial, denoted by \(I_L\), and then by the Newton polynomial, denoted by \(I_N\). Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: No definite relation exists between \(I_L\) and \(I_N\)

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: No definite relation exists between \(I_L\) and \(I_N\)
structuredOptions.html: No definite relation exists between \(I_L\) and \(I_N\)

questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Function \(f(x)\) given at \(n\) distinct values.
    • Lagrange polynomial estimate at point \(x^*\) is \(I_L\).
    • Newton polynomial estimate at point \(x^*\) is \(I_N\).
  • Aim: Determine the relationship between \(I_L\) and \(I_N\).

3. Core Concepts:

Uniqueness Theorem of Polynomial Interpolation: According to the fundamental theorem of algebra, for any set of \(n\) distinct data points \((x_1, y_1), (x_2, y_2), \dots, (x_n, y_n)\), there exists exactly one unique polynomial of degree at most \(n-1\) that passes precisely through all these points.

4. Solution Method:

Lagrange interpolation and Newton divided-difference interpolation are just two different algebraic formulations to arrive at the interpolating polynomial. Since the interpolating polynomial through a specific set of distinct points is unique, both methods yield the exact same polynomial curve. Therefore, evaluated at any arbitrary point \(x^*\), the numerical estimates will be identical.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Recognize that Lagrange and Newton forms both build a polynomial of degree \(n-1\).
  2. Apply the Uniqueness Theorem: \(P_{\text{Lagrange}}(x) \equiv P_{\text{Newton}}(x)\).
  3. Conclude that for any \(x = x^*\), the output \(I_L\) equals \(I_N\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(I_L\) and \(I_N\) are always equal | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q26
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The probability density function of a continuous random variable distributed uniformly between x and y (for y > x) is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability and Statistics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • A continuous random variable
    • Follows a uniform distribution
    • Defined on the interval between \(x\) and \(y\) (with \(y > x\))
  • Aim: Identify the mathematical expression for the Probability Density Function (PDF) of this distribution.

3. Core Concepts:

Uniform Probability Distribution: A continuous uniform distribution, often denoted as \(U(a, b)\), describes a random variable that has an equally likely chance of assuming any value within a defined interval \([a, b]\).

Probability Density Function (PDF): The area under the PDF curve across the entire domain must strictly equal 1, i.e., \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(t)\, dt = 1\). For a uniform distribution shaped as a rectangle over the interval \([a, b]\), the height \(f(t)\) must be constant.

Formula: The height of the rectangle (the PDF) is the reciprocal of the base length:

\[f(t) = \dfrac{1}{\text{upper limit} - \text{lower limit}} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Identify the lower boundary (\(a\)) and upper boundary (\(b\)).
  2. Substitute the given boundary variables (\(x\) and \(y\)) into the standard uniform distribution formula.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. The problem states the variable is distributed between \(x\) and \(y\), and explicitly defines \(y > x\).
  2. The lower bound \(a = x\).
  3. The upper bound \(b = y\).
  4. The base length of the distribution interval is \((b - a) = (y - x)\).
  5. Substitute into the PDF formula:\[f(t) = \dfrac{1}{b - a} = \dfrac{1}{y - x} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{1}{y - x}\) | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q27
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: Consider the hemi-spherical tank of radius 13 m as shown in the figure (not drawn to scale). What is the volume of water (in m³) when the depth of water at the centre of the tank is 6 m?
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics & Mathematics | Geometry of Solids

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Shape of the tank: Hemispherical
    • Radius of the tank, \(R = 13\) m
    • Depth of water at the center, \(h = 6\) m
  • Aim: Calculate the exact volume of water in the tank in m³.

3. Core Concepts:

Volume of a Spherical Cap: When a sphere (or hemisphere) is partially filled, the filled portion forms a geometric shape known as a "spherical cap."

Derivation/Formula: The volume \(V\) of a spherical cap of height \(h\) in a sphere of radius \(R\) is derived from the solid of revolution:

\[V = \int_{0}^{h} \pi r^2\, dy \]

Using the equation of a circle \(x^2 + (y - R)^2 = R^2 \implies x^2 = 2Ry - y^2\), the integrated formula becomes:

\[V = \dfrac{\pi h^2}{3}(3R - h) \]

4. Solution Method:

Directly apply the spherical cap volume formula using the provided dimensions.

Common Pitfall: Students often accidentally use the full hemisphere volume formula \(\dfrac{2}{3}\pi R^3\) and scale it linearly by depth (e.g., \(\dfrac{6}{13} \times V_{\text{total}}\)), which is incorrect because the cross-sectional area of a sphere varies quadratically, not linearly.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Note the known variables: \(R = 13\) m, \(h = 6\) m.
  2. Step 2: Substitute into the spherical cap formula:\[ V = \dfrac{\pi (6)^2}{3} \times [3(13) - 6] \]
  3. Step 3: Compute the squared term and simplify the fraction:\[V = \dfrac{36\pi}{3} \times (39 - 6) = 12\pi \times 33 \]
  4. Step 4: Multiply the final constants:\[V = 396\pi \text{ m}^3 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(396\pi\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q28
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
An ordinary differential equation is given below.

\[\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)(x \ln x) = y\]

The solution for the above equation is
(Note: K denotes a constant in the options)
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Differential equation: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}(x \ln x) = y\)
  • Aim: Find the general solution of the ODE (where \(K\) represents the constant of integration).

3. Core Concepts:

Separation of Variables: A first-order ODE of the form \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = g(x)h(y)\) can be solved algebraically by isolating all terms involving \(y\) (including \(dy\)) on one side and all terms involving \(x\) (including \(dx\)) on the other side.

Logarithmic Integration Rule: \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\, dx = \ln|f(x)| + C\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Rearrange the equation to group \(y\)-terms on the left and \(x\)-terms on the right.
  2. Integrate both sides with respect to their respective variables.
  3. Use \(u\)-substitution for the right-hand side integration.
  4. Simplify using logarithmic properties to solve for \(y\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Rearrange the ODE.\[\dfrac{dy}{y} = \dfrac{dx}{x \ln x} \]
  2. Step 2: Apply the integral operator to both sides.\[\int \dfrac{1}{y}\, dy = \int \dfrac{1}{x \ln x}\, dx \]
  3. Step 3: Evaluate the left-hand side integral.\[\text{LHS} = \ln y \]
  4. Step 4: Evaluate the right-hand side integral using substitution.
    Let \(u = \ln x\). Differentiating gives \(du = \dfrac{1}{x}\, dx\).\[\text{RHS} = \int \dfrac{1}{u}\, du = \ln u + C \]Substitute back \(u = \ln x\):\[\text{RHS} = \ln(\ln x) + C \]
  5. Step 5: Equate LHS and RHS and solve for \(y\).
    Let the integration constant \(C = \ln K\) (since \(K\) is just an arbitrary positive constant).\[\ln y = \ln(\ln x) + \ln K \]Combine the logarithms on the RHS using \(\ln a + \ln b = \ln(ab)\):\[\ln y = \ln(K \ln x) \implies y = K \ln x \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(y = K \ln x\) | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q35
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The inverse of the matrix \(\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 4 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\) is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given Data: Matrix \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 4 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\)
  • Aim: Determine the inverse matrix, \(A^{-1}\).

3. Core Concepts:

Inverse of a Matrix: \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{\text{Adj}(A)}{|A|}\)

Determinant (\(|A|\)): Expanded along the first row: \(|A| = a_{11}C_{11} + a_{12}C_{12} + a_{13}C_{13}\)

Cofactor (\(C_{ij}\)): \(C_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j} M_{ij}\) (where \(M_{ij}\) is the minor determinant).

4. Solution Method & Execution:

  1. Step 1: Find the Determinant \(|A|\)\[|A| = 2(3 \times 4 - 1 \times 2) - 3(4 \times 4 - 1 \times 1) + 4(4 \times 2 - 3 \times 1) \]\[= 2(10) - 3(15) + 4(5) = 20 - 45 + 20 = -5 \]
  2. Step 2: Evaluate cofactors of first row (to isolate the right option)
    • \(C_{11} = +(12 - 2) = 10\)
    • \(C_{12} = -(16 - 1) = -15\)
    • \(C_{13} = +(8 - 3) = 5\)
    Since \(\text{Adj}(A) = C^T\), the first column of the Adjoint Matrix is \(\begin{bmatrix} 10 \\ -15 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}\).
    Dividing by \(|A| = -5\), the first column of the inverse is \(\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}\).
    Checking the options: (C) and (D) both match this first column — need one more element to distinguish.
  3. Step 3: Evaluate \(C_{22}\) to distinguish between options\[C_{22} = +((2 \times 4) - (4 \times 1)) = 8 - 4 = 4 \]Element \((2,2)\) of \(A^{-1}\) is \(\dfrac{C_{22}}{|A|} = \dfrac{4}{-5} = -\dfrac{4}{5}\).
    Option (C) has \(-\dfrac{4}{5}\) at position \((2,2)\); option (D) has \(+\dfrac{4}{5}\). → Option (C) is correct.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 4/5 & 9/5 \\ 3 & -4/5 & -14/5 \\ -1 & 1/5 & 6/5 \end{bmatrix}\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2019 Set 2 | CE Q43
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: A series of perpendicular offsets taken from a curved boundary wall to a straight survey line at an interval of 6 m are 1.22, 1.67, 2.04, 2.34, 2.14, 1.87, and 1.15 m. The area (in m², round off to 2 decimal places) bounded by the survey line, curved boundary wall, the first and the last offsets, determined using Simpson’s rule, is ______
questions.explanation:
Surveying | Area & Volume Computations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Series of perpendicular offsets: \(O_1 = 1.22\) m, \(O_2 = 1.67\) m, \(O_3 = 2.04\) m, \(O_4 = 2.34\) m, \(O_5 = 2.14\) m, \(O_6 = 1.87\) m, \(O_7 = 1.15\) m
    • Interval between offsets (\(d\)): 6 m
    • Total number of offsets (\(n\)): 7
  • Aim: Calculate the total area using Simpson's rule, rounded to 2 decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

Simpson's One-Third Rule: Used to determine the area of irregular tracts. It assumes the boundary between consecutive offset intervals is a parabolic arc.

\[ \text{Area} = \dfrac{d}{3}\left[(O_1 + O_n) + 4(O_2 + O_4 + \dots + O_{n-1}) + 2(O_3 + O_5 + \dots + O_{n-2})\right] \]

Condition for Application: The rule is strictly applicable only when the total number of offsets (\(n\)) is odd (i.e., the number of intervals is even). Here \(n = 7\), so the condition is satisfied perfectly.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Verify the number of offsets is odd.
  2. Group the offsets into: first & last, even-numbered, and remaining odd-numbered.
  3. Compute the sum of each group.
  4. Apply Simpson's one-third rule formula to find the total area.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Identify and categorize offsets
    • \(d = 6\) m
    • First and Last: \(O_1 = 1.22\) m, \(O_7 = 1.15\) m
    • Even-indexed: \(O_2 = 1.67\) m, \(O_4 = 2.34\) m, \(O_6 = 1.87\) m
    • Odd-indexed (excluding first and last): \(O_3 = 2.04\) m, \(O_5 = 2.14\) m
  2. Step 2: Calculate subgroup sums
    • \((O_1 + O_7) = 1.22 + 1.15 = 2.37\) m
    • \((O_2 + O_4 + O_6) = 1.67 + 2.34 + 1.87 = 5.88\) m
    • \((O_3 + O_5) = 2.04 + 2.14 = 4.18\) m
  3. Step 3: Apply Simpson's Rule\[ \text{Area} = \dfrac{6}{3} \times [2.37 + 4(5.88) + 2(4.18)] \]\[ = 2 \times [2.37 + 23.52 + 8.36] = 2 \times 34.25 = 68.50\text{ m}^2 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 68.50 m² | Accepted key range: 67.00 to 70.00

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q2
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
For the given orthogonal matrix Q,
\[Q = \begin{bmatrix} 3/7 & 2/7 & 6/7 \\ -6/7 & 3/7 & 2/7 \\ 2/7 & 6/7 & -3/7 \end{bmatrix} \]
The inverse is
questions.explanation:
Linear Algebra (Matrices) | Orthogonal Matrices

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data: Orthogonal matrix \(\mathbf{Q}\) where \(\mathbf{Q}^{-1} = \mathbf{Q}^T\)
  • Aim: Find \(\mathbf{Q}^{-1}\).

3. Core Concepts:

Orthogonal Matrix Property: For an orthogonal matrix, the inverse equals the transpose (rows become columns):

\[\mathbf{Q}^{-1} = \mathbf{Q}^T \]

Given:

\[\mathbf{Q} = \begin{bmatrix} 3/7 & 2/7 & 6/7 \\ -6/7 & 3/7 & 2/7 \\ 2/7 & 6/7 & -3/7 \end{bmatrix} \]

4. Solution Method:

Simply transpose \(\mathbf{Q}\) — convert rows to columns.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Original Matrix \(\mathbf{Q}\):

Column 1Column 2Column 3
Row 1\(3/7\)\(2/7\)\(6/7\)
Row 2\(-6/7\)\(3/7\)\(2/7\)
Row 3\(2/7\)\(6/7\)\(-3/7\)

Transpose \(\mathbf{Q}^T\) (Rows ↔ Columns):

Column 1Column 2Column 3
Row 1\(3/7\)\(-6/7\)\(2/7\)
Row 2\(2/7\)\(3/7\)\(6/7\)
Row 3\(6/7\)\(2/7\)\(-3/7\)

Verification of Orthogonality: Check \(\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{Q}^T = \mathbf{I}\)

  • Row 1 · Row 1: \((3/7)^2 + (2/7)^2 + (6/7)^2 = (9+4+36)/49 = 1\) ✓
  • Row 1 · Row 2: \((3/7)(-6/7) + (2/7)(3/7) + (6/7)(2/7) = (-18+6+12)/49 = 0\) ✓

6. Final Answer:

\[\mathbf{Q}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 3/7 & -6/7 & 2/7 \\ 2/7 & 3/7 & 6/7 \\ 6/7 & 2/7 & -3/7 \end{bmatrix} \]

Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q3
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: At the point \( x = 0 \), the function \( f(x) = x^3 \) has
options: neither local maximum nor local minimum

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: neither local maximum nor local minimum
structuredOptions.html: neither local maximum nor local minimum

questions.explanation:
Calculus (Differential Calculus) | Critical Points & Extrema

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: \(f(x) = x^3\) at \(x = 0\)
  • Aim: Determine the nature of the critical point at \(x = 0\).

3. Core Concepts:

First Derivative Test: \(f'(x) = 0\) gives a critical point. A sign change in \(f'(x)\) determines max/min.

Second Derivative Test:

  • \(f''(x) > 0\) → Local minimum
  • \(f''(x) < 0\) → Local maximum
  • \(f''(x) = 0\) → Test fails (point of inflection possible)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Find \(f'(x)\) and locate critical points.
  2. Apply higher-order derivative test when \(f''(x) = 0\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: First Derivative\[f'(x) = 3x^2 \]At \(x = 0\): \(f'(0) = 0\) → Critical point confirmed.
  2. Step 2: Second Derivative\[f''(x) = 6x \]At \(x = 0\): \(f''(0) = 0\) → Test inconclusive!
  3. Step 3: Higher-Order Test (Third Derivative)\[f'''(x) = 6 \neq 0 \]Since the first non-zero derivative is of odd order (3rd), \(x = 0\) is a point of inflection, not an extremum.
  4. Step 4: Sign Analysis of \(f'(x)\)
    Interval\(x\)\(f'(x) = 3x^2\)Sign
    \(x < 0\)\(-1\)\(3(1) = 3\)+
    \(x > 0\)\(+1\)\(3(1) = 3\)+

    \(f'(x) > 0\) on both sides → No sign change → No local max or min.

    Graphical Insight: \(f(x) = x^3\) is strictly increasing everywhere with a horizontal tangent at the origin (inflection point).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Neither local maximum nor local minimum | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q26
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The value of the integral \(\displaystyle \int_0^{\pi} x \cos^2 x \, dx \) is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Integral Calculus

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Definite integral: \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi} x \cos^2 x \, dx\)
  • Aim: Evaluate the exact value of the given definite integral.

3. Core Concepts:

Property of Definite Integrals (King's Rule):

\[\int_{0}^{a} f(x) \, dx = \int_{0}^{a} f(a - x) \, dx \]

This property is exceptionally useful for removing the algebraic multiplier \(x\) from trigonometric integrands.

Trigonometric Identities:

\(\cos(\pi - \theta) = -\cos\theta \implies \cos^2(\pi - \theta) = \cos^2\theta\)

\(\cos^2 x = \dfrac{1 + \cos(2x)}{2}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Let the given integral be \(I\).
  2. Apply the King's Rule to substitute \(x\) with \((\pi - x)\).
  3. Add the original integral and the new integral. The variable \(x\) will cancel out, leaving a simpler trigonometric integral multiplied by \(\pi\).
  4. Use the double-angle identity for \(\cos^2 x\) to evaluate the resulting integral.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Define the integral.\[I = \int_{0}^{\pi} x \cos^2 x \, dx \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)} \]
  2. Step 2: Apply the property \(\displaystyle \int_{0}^{a} f(x) \, dx = \int_{0}^{a} f(a - x) \, dx\).\[I = \int_{0}^{\pi} (\pi - x) \cos^2(\pi - x) \, dx \]Since \(\cos(\pi - x) = -\cos x\), squaring gives \(\cos^2 x\).\[I = \int_{0}^{\pi} (\pi - x) \cos^2 x \, dx \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)} \]
  3. Step 3: Add Equation 1 and Equation 2.\[I + I = \int_{0}^{\pi} x \cos^2 x \, dx + \int_{0}^{\pi} (\pi - x) \cos^2 x \, dx \]\[2I = \int_{0}^{\pi} (x + \pi - x) \cos^2 x \, dx \]\[2I = \pi \int_{0}^{\pi} \cos^2 x \, dx \]
  4. Step 4: Substitute the trigonometric identity for \(\cos^2 x\).\[2I = \pi \int_{0}^{\pi} \left( \dfrac{1 + \cos 2x}{2} \right) dx \]\[ 2I = \dfrac{\pi}{2} \left[x + \dfrac{\sin 2x}{2} \right]_{0}^{\pi} \]
  5. Step 5: Evaluate the limits.\[ 2I = \dfrac{\pi}{2} \left[\left(\pi + \dfrac{\sin 2\pi}{2}\right) - \left(0 + \dfrac{\sin 0}{2}\right) \right] \]Knowing that \(\sin 2\pi = 0\) and \(\sin 0 = 0\):\[ 2I = \dfrac{\pi}{2} [\pi + 0 - 0 - 0] \]\[2I = \dfrac{\pi^2}{2} \implies I = \dfrac{\pi^2}{4} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{\pi^2}{4}\) | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q37
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The solution at \( x = 1, t = 1 \) of the partial differential equation \( \dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} = 25 \dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} \) subject to initial conditions of \( u(0) = 3x \) and \( \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial t}(0) = 3 \) is _______
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Partial Differential Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • PDE: \(\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} = 25 \dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}\)
    • Initial displacement: \(u(x,0) = 3x\)
    • Initial velocity: \(\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial t}(x,0) = 3\)
  • Aim: Find the value of \(u(x,t)\) at \(x = 1,\ t = 1\).

3. Core Concepts:

1D Wave Equation: The standard form is \(\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}\).

D'Alembert's Solution: For an infinite string with initial displacement \(f(x)\) and initial velocity \(g(x)\):

\[ u(x,t) = \dfrac{1}{2}[f(x-ct) + f(x+ct)] + \dfrac{1}{2c} \int_{x-ct}^{x+ct} g(s)\, ds \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Rearrange the given PDE to standard form to find the wave speed \(c\).
  2. Identify the functions \(f(x)\) and \(g(x)\) from the initial conditions.
  3. Substitute \(x=1,\ t=1\) and compute the function values and the integral.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Determine wave speed \(c\)
    Given: \(\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} = 25\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} \implies \dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} = \dfrac{1}{25}\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}\)
    Comparing with standard form: \(c^2 = \dfrac{1}{25} \implies c = \dfrac{1}{5}\)
  2. Step 2: Identify initial conditions
    \(f(x) = u(x,0) = 3x\)
    \(g(x) = \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial t}(x,0) = 3\)
  3. Step 3: Apply D'Alembert's Equation at \(x=1,\ t=1\)\[ u(1,1) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[f\!\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right) + f\!\left(\dfrac{6}{5}\right)\right] + \dfrac{5}{2}\int_{4/5}^{6/5} 3\, ds \]
  4. Step 4: Evaluate each term
    Displacement part:
    \(f(4/5) = 3(4/5) = 12/5\)
    \(f(6/5) = 3(6/5) = 18/5\)\[ \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{12}{5} + \dfrac{18}{5}\right] = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 6 = 3 \]Velocity part:\[ \dfrac{5}{2}[3s]_{4/5}^{6/5} = \dfrac{15}{2}\left(\dfrac{6}{5} - \dfrac{4}{5}\right) = \dfrac{15}{2} \times \dfrac{2}{5} = 3 \]
  5. Step 5: Final sum\[u(1,1) = 3 + 3 = 6 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 6 | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q38
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The solution (up to three decimal places) at \( x = 1 \) of the differential equation \( \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 2\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0 \) subject to boundary conditions \( y(0) = 1 \) and \( \dfrac{dy}{dx}(0) = -1 \) is _______
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Ordinary Differential Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • ODE: \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 2\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0\)
    • Boundary Conditions: \(y(0) = 1\) and \(y'(0) = -1\)
  • Aim: Find the solution \(y(1)\) up to three decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

Linear Homogeneous 2nd Order ODEs: Solved by finding the roots of the characteristic (auxiliary) equation \(am^2 + bm + c = 0\).

Repeated Roots: If roots \(m_1 = m_2 = m\), the general solution is: \(y(x) = (C_1 + C_2 x)e^{mx}\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Write the characteristic equation and find its roots.
  2. Form the general solution \(y(x)\).
  3. Use \(y(0) = 1\) to find \(C_1\).
  4. Differentiate \(y(x)\) and use \(y'(0) = -1\) to find \(C_2\).
  5. Evaluate the particular solution at \(x = 1\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Characteristic Equation\[m^2 + 2m + 1 = 0 \implies (m+1)^2 = 0 \implies m = -1,\ -1 \]
  2. Step 2: General Solution\[y(x) = (C_1 + C_2 x)e^{-x} \]
  3. Step 3: Apply \(y(0) = 1\)\[y(0) = (C_1 + 0)e^0 = C_1 \implies C_1 = 1 \]
  4. Step 4: Apply \(y'(0) = -1\)
    Differentiating using the product rule:\[y'(x) = C_2 e^{-x} - (C_1 + C_2 x)e^{-x} \]Substituting \(x=0,\ C_1=1\):\[y'(0) = C_2 - 1 = -1 \implies C_2 = 0 \]
  5. Step 5: Particular solution evaluated at \(x=1\)
    With \(C_1 = 1,\ C_2 = 0\):\[y(x) = e^{-x} \]\[y(1) = e^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{e} \approx 0.367879 \approx 0.368 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.368 | Accepted key range: 0.36 to 0.37

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 1 | CE Q39
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Variation of water depth (y) in a gradually varied open channel flow is given by the first order differential equation

\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1 - e^{-\frac{10}{3}\ln(y)}}{250 - 45e^{-3\ln(y)}} \]

Given initial condition: \( y(x = 0) = 0.8 \text{ m} \). The depth (in m, up to three decimal places) of flow at a downstream section at \( x = 1 \text{ m} \) from one calculation step of Single Step Euler Method is _______
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • ODE: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1 - e^{-\dfrac{10}{3}\ln(y)}}{250 - 45e^{-3\ln(y)}}\)
    • Initial condition: \(y(0) = 0.8 \text{ m}\)
    • Step size: \(h = 1\) m (one calculation step from \(x=0\) to \(x=1\))
  • Aim: Find \(y(1)\) using the Single Step Euler Method.

3. Core Concepts:

Euler's Forward Method:

\[y_{i+1} = y_i + h \cdot f(x_i, y_i) \]

Logarithmic Identity: \(e^{k\ln(y)} = y^k\). This simplifies the expression significantly.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Simplify \(f(x,y)\) using logarithmic properties.
  2. Evaluate the slope \(f(x_0, y_0)\) at \(x_0 = 0,\ y_0 = 0.8\).
  3. Apply Euler's formula to find \(y_1\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Simplify \(f(x,y)\)\[f(x,y) = \dfrac{1 - y^{-10/3}}{250 - 45y^{-3}} \]
  2. Step 2: Evaluate at \(y_0 = 0.8\)
    Numerator component: \((0.8)^{-10/3} = (1.25)^{10/3} \approx 2.10444\)
    Denominator component: \((0.8)^{-3} = (1.25)^3 = 1.953125\)\[f(0,\ 0.8) = \dfrac{1 - 2.10444}{250 - 45 \times 1.953125} = \dfrac{-1.10444}{250 - 87.8906} = \dfrac{-1.10444}{162.109} \approx -0.006813 \]
  3. Step 3: Euler's Method step\[y(1) = 0.8 + 1 \times (-0.006813) = 0.793187 \approx 0.793 \text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.793 | Accepted key range: 0.78 to 0.80

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q3

questions.question:
A probability distribution with right skew is shown in the figure.



The correct statement for the probability distribution is

Mean is greater than median and mode

structuredOptions.label: B

questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability and Statistics — Skewness

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: A graphical plot of a probability distribution \(f(x)\) vs \(x\) with a long tail extending to the right (Right Skew).
  • Aim: Identify the correct relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode.

3. Core Concepts:

Right-Skewed (Positively Skewed) Distribution: Mass concentrated on the left; long tail extending to the right driven by positive outliers.

Positions of Central Tendencies:

  • Mode: \(x\)-value at the peak (maximum frequency) — far left.
  • Mean: Heavily influenced by extreme tail values — pulled far right.
  • Median: Splits area in half (50th percentile) — lies between Mode and Mean.

Empirical Rule for Right Skew: \(\text{Mean} > \text{Median} > \text{Mode}\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify the distribution as right-skewed from the graph (long tail to the right).
  2. Mode = peak (leftmost); Mean = pulled rightward by tail; Median = between Mode and Mean.
  3. Moving left to right: Mode → Median → Mean, giving \(\text{Mean} > \text{Median} > \text{Mode}\).
  4. Evaluate options:
    • (A) Mean = Mode → False (symmetric distribution)
    • (B) Mean > Median but < Mode → False
    • (C) Mean > Median and Mean > Mode → True ✓
    • (D) Mode > Median → False (indicates left skew)

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Mean is greater than median and mode | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q19

questions.question: Probability (up to one decimal place) of consecutively picking 3 red balls without replacement from a box containing 5 red balls and 1 white ball is ______
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability Theory — Sampling Without Replacement

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Red balls = 5, White balls = 1; Total = 6; 3 balls drawn consecutively without replacement.
  • Aim: Calculate the probability that all 3 drawn balls are red.

3. Core Concepts:

Conditional Probability (without replacement):\[P(\text{3 red}) = \dfrac{R}{T} \times \dfrac{R-1}{T-1} \times \dfrac{R-2}{T-2}\]where \(R\) = red balls, \(T\) = total balls.

Alternative (Combinatorial): \(\dfrac{\binom{5}{3}}{\binom{6}{3}}\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Initial state: 5 red, 1 white → Total = 6
    \(P_1 = \dfrac{5}{6}\)
  2. After 1 red drawn: 4 red, 1 white → Total = 5
    \(P_2 = \dfrac{4}{5}\)
  3. After 2 red drawn: 3 red, 1 white → Total = 4
    \(P_3 = \dfrac{3}{4}\)
  4. Combined probability:\[P = \dfrac{5}{6} \times \dfrac{4}{5} \times \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{60}{120} = 0.5\]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.5 | Accepted range: 0.5 to 0.5

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q20
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The quadratic equation \( 2x^2 - 3x + 3 = 0 \) is to be solved numerically starting with an initial guess as \( x_0 = 2 \). The new estimate of \( x \) after the first iteration using Newton-Raphson method is ______
questions.explanation:
Numerical Methods | Newton-Raphson Method for Root Finding

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Equation \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 3x + 3 = 0\); initial guess \(x_0 = 2\); first iteration of Newton-Raphson.
  • Aim: Find the new estimate \(x_1\).

3. Core Concepts:

Newton-Raphson Formula:\[x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}\]

Function and derivative:\[f(x) = 2x^2 - 3x + 3 \qquad f'(x) = 4x - 3\]

Note: Discriminant \(= (-3)^2 - 4(2)(3) = -15 < 0\) (no real roots), but the iteration is still computable.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Evaluate at \(x_0 = 2\):\[f(2) = 2(4) - 3(2) + 3 = 8 - 6 + 3 = 5\]\[f'(2) = 4(2) - 3 = 8 - 3 = 5\]
  2. Apply Newton-Raphson formula:\[x_1 = 2 - \dfrac{5}{5} = 2 - 1 = 1\]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1 | Accepted range: 1 to 1

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q26
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The matrix \( \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -4 \\ 4 & -2 \end{pmatrix} \) has
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: A \(2 \times 2\) matrix \(A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -4 \\ 4 & -2 \end{pmatrix}\)
  • Aim: To determine the nature (real or complex) of the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the given matrix.

3. Core Concepts:

Eigenvalues (\(\lambda\)) of a matrix \(A\) are the roots of its characteristic equation: \(\det(A - \lambda I) = 0\).

For a \(2 \times 2\) matrix, the characteristic equation simplifies to: \(\lambda^2 - \text{Tr}(A)\lambda + \det(A) = 0\), where \(\text{Tr}(A)\) is the trace (sum of principal diagonal elements) and \(\det(A)\) is the determinant.

Fundamental Theorem: If a real matrix has complex eigenvalues, the corresponding eigenvectors must also be complex because solving the system \((A - \lambda I)x = 0\) inherently involves complex arithmetic.

4. Solution Method:

  • Compute the trace and determinant of the matrix.
  • Form the characteristic equation and solve for \(\lambda\) to find the eigenvalues.
  • Evaluate whether the roots are real or complex.
  • Infer the nature of the eigenvectors based on the eigenvalues.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Trace of \(A\): \(\text{Tr}(A) = 2 + (-2) = 0\)
  2. Determinant of \(A\): \(\det(A) = (2)(-2) - (-4)(4) = -4 + 16 = 12\)
  3. Characteristic Equation:\[\lambda^2 - 0\cdot\lambda + 12 = 0 \implies \lambda^2 = -12\]
  4. Solve for \(\lambda\):\[\lambda = \pm \sqrt{-12} = \pm i2\sqrt{3}\]Since the discriminant is negative, \(\lambda\) contains an imaginary part \(i\). Thus, the eigenvalues are complex.
  5. Determine Eigenvector Nature: The matrix \(A\) consists purely of real entries. Finding the eigenvector involves finding the null space of \((A - \lambda I)\). Because \(\lambda\) is complex, the resulting matrix \((A - \lambda I)\) will have complex entries, enforcing the resulting null space vectors (eigenvectors) to be complex.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Complex eigenvalues and eigenvectors | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q27
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The Laplace transform \( F(s) \) of the exponential function, \( f(t) = e^{at} \) when \( t \ge 0 \), where \( a \) is a constant and \( (s-a) > 0 \), is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus (Laplace Transforms)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data: Function \(f(t) = e^{at}\) for \(t \ge 0\), along with the condition \((s - a) > 0\).
  • Aim: To find the unilateral Laplace transform \(F(s)\) of the exponential function.

3. Core Concepts:

Unilateral Laplace Transform Definition: \(F(s) = L\{f(t)\} = \int_0^\infty f(t) e^{-st} dt\)

Region of Convergence (ROC): The condition \((s - a) > 0\) or \(s > a\) guarantees that the integral converges to a finite value as \(t \to \infty\).

4. Solution Method:

  • Substitute \(f(t) = e^{at}\) directly into the integral definition.
  • Combine the exponential terms.
  • Perform the definite integration from \(0\) to \(\infty\), strictly applying limits to verify the use of the constraint.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Set up the integral:\[F(s) = \int_0^\infty e^{at} \cdot e^{-st}\, dt\]
  2. Combine exponents:\[F(s) = \int_0^\infty e^{-(s-a)t}\, dt\]
  3. Integrate:\[F(s) = \left[\dfrac{e^{-(s-a)t}}{-(s-a)} \right]_0^\infty\]
  4. Apply limits:
    • Upper limit (\(t \to \infty\)): Because \((s-a) > 0\), the exponent \(-(s-a)t\) becomes an increasingly large negative number, so \(e^{-\infty} \to 0\).
    • Lower limit (\(t = 0\)): \(e^{-(s-a) \cdot 0} = e^0 = 1\).
  5. Evaluate:\[F(s) = 0 - \left( \dfrac{1}{-(s-a)} \right) = \dfrac{1}{s-a}\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{1}{s-a}\) | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q28

questions.question:
The rank of the following matrix is
\( \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 3 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \)
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra (Matrices)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: A \(3 \times 4\) matrix \(A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 3 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\)
  • Aim: To determine the rank of the matrix.

3. Core Concepts:

The Rank of a matrix is the maximum number of linearly independent row or column vectors it contains.

It is determined by converting the matrix into an upper triangular (Row Echelon) form using elementary row operations and counting the number of non-zero rows.

4. Solution Method:

  • Apply Gaussian elimination sequentially to eliminate elements below the main diagonal.
  • Track dependencies to deduce row echelon form.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Initial matrix (rows \(R_1, R_2, R_3\)):\[\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 3 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\]
  2. Eliminate the first column below \(R_1\):
    • \(R_2 \rightarrow R_2 - 2R_1\): \(\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -2 & 2 & 6 \end{pmatrix}\)
    • \(R_3 \rightarrow R_3 - 4R_1\): \(\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -3 & 3 & 9 \end{pmatrix}\)
    Updated matrix:\[\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 & 9 \end{pmatrix}\]
  3. Simplify \(R_2\) and \(R_3\):
    • \(R_2 \rightarrow R_2 / (-2) \implies \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & -1 & -3 \end{pmatrix}\)
    • \(R_3 \rightarrow R_3 / (-3) \implies \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & -1 & -3 \end{pmatrix}\)
  4. Eliminate the second column below \(R_2\):
    • \(R_3 \rightarrow R_3 - R_2 \implies \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\)
    Final Echelon form:\[\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\]
  5. Determine Rank: There are exactly 2 non-zero rows remaining. Therefore, the rank is 2.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2 | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q37
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The value (up to two decimal places) of a line integral \(\displaystyle \int_C \vec{F}(\vec{r}) \cdot d\vec{r} \), for \( \vec{F}(\vec{r}) = x^2\hat{i} + y^2\hat{j} \) along C which is a straight line joining (0,0) to (1,1) is ______
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Vector Calculus

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Vector Field: \(\vec{F}(\vec{r}) = x^2\,\hat{i} + y^2\,\hat{j}\)
    • Path of integration \(C\): Straight line joining points \((0,0)\) to \((1,1)\)
  • Aim: Evaluate the line integral \(\displaystyle\int_C \vec{F}(\vec{r}) \cdot d\vec{r}\) up to two decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

Work Done / Line Integral:\[\int_C \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r} = \int_C (F_x\,dx + F_y\,dy)\]

Parametrization of a Line: For a straight line joining the origin to point \((1,1)\), the equation of the path is \(y = x\). Therefore, \(dy = dx\).

Sanity Check: The vector field is conservative because \(\nabla \times \vec{F} = 0\). The integral is path-independent, making direct evaluation along \(y = x\) fully valid.

4. Solution Method:

Substitute the equation of the line (\(y = x\) and \(dy = dx\)) into the line integral formula to convert it into a single-variable definite integral, then solve.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Set up the differential path vector:\[d\vec{r} = dx\,\hat{i} + dy\,\hat{j}\]
  2. Form the dot product:\[\vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r} = (x^2\,\hat{i} + y^2\,\hat{j}) \cdot (dx\,\hat{i} + dy\,\hat{j}) = x^2\,dx + y^2\,dy\]
  3. Apply path parametrization (\(y = x\), \(dy = dx\)):\[\int_C \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r} = \int_{x=0}^{x=1} (x^2\,dx + x^2\,dx) = \int_{0}^{1} 2x^2\,dx\]
  4. Integrate and evaluate bounds:\[= \left[\dfrac{2x^3}{3} \right]_{0}^{1} = \dfrac{2(1)^3}{3} - 0 = \dfrac{2}{3} \approx 0.67\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.67 | Accepted key range: 0.60 to 0.70

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q1
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The matrix \(\mathbf{P}\) is the inverse of a matrix \(\mathbf{Q}\). If \(\mathbf{I}\) denotes the identity matrix, which one of the following options is correct?
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra / Matrices

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Matrix \(\mathbf{P}\) is the inverse of matrix \(\mathbf{Q}\); \(\mathbf{I}\) denotes the identity matrix.
  • Aim: Identify the correct relationship between \(\mathbf{P}\), \(\mathbf{Q}\), and \(\mathbf{I}\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Definition of Matrix Inverse: For a square matrix \(\mathbf{Q}\), if inverse \(\mathbf{P}\) exists, then \(\mathbf{Q} imes \mathbf{P}\) yields the identity matrix \(\mathbf{I}\).
  • Commutativity of Inverses: Although matrix multiplication is generally not commutative, a matrix and its inverse do commute:
    \[\mathbf{P} = \mathbf{Q}^{-1} \iff \mathbf{PQ} = \mathbf{QP} = \mathbf{I} \]

4. Solution Method:

From \(\mathbf{P} = \mathbf{Q}^{-1}\), multiply both sides by \(\mathbf{Q}\) on the right and on the left to verify both products equal \(\mathbf{I}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Option (A): \(\mathbf{PQ} = \mathbf{I}\) but \(\mathbf{QP} eq \mathbf{I}\) — Incorrect (they must commute).
  2. Option (B): \(\mathbf{QP} = \mathbf{I}\) but \(\mathbf{PQ} eq \mathbf{I}\) — Incorrect.
  3. Option (C): \(\mathbf{PQ} = \mathbf{I}\) and \(\mathbf{QP} = \mathbf{I}\) — Correct.
  4. Option (D): \(\mathbf{PQ} - \mathbf{QP} = \mathbf{I} \implies \mathbf{I} - \mathbf{I} = \mathbf{0} eq \mathbf{I}\) — Incorrect.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\mathbf{PQ} = \mathbf{I}\) and \(\mathbf{QP} = \mathbf{I}\)  |  Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q2
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The number of parameters in the univariate exponential and Gaussian distributions, respectively, are
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability and Statistics / Probability Distributions

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Two distributions — Univariate Exponential and Gaussian (Normal).
  • Aim: Determine the number of independent parameters required to fully define each distribution.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Univariate Exponential Distribution: Models the time elapsed between events in a Poisson process.
    PDF: \(f(x) = \lambda e^{-\lambda x}\) for \(x \ge 0\).
    Defined by one parameter: the rate \(\lambda\).
  • Gaussian (Normal) Distribution: Models continuous data clustering around a central mean.
    PDF: \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp\!\left(-\dfrac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)\)
    Defined by two parameters: mean \(\mu\) and variance \(\sigma^2\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Exponential parameters = 1 (\(\lambda\)).
  2. Gaussian parameters = 2 (\(\mu,\ \sigma\)).
  3. Sequence (Exponential, Gaussian) \(\rightarrow\) 1 and 2.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1 and 2  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q3
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: Let \(x\) be a continuous variable defined over the interval \((-\infty, \infty)\), and \(f(x) = e^{-x} - e^{-x}\). The integral \(g(x) = \displaystyle \int f(x) \, dx\) is equal to
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus / Integrals

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: \(x \in (-\infty,\infty)\); function \(f(x) = e^{-x - e^{-x}}\)
    Correction Note: OCR may parse the function as \(e^{-x} - e^{-x}\) (which equals 0). The correct form, visible in the screenshot, is the nested exponent \(f(x) = e^{-x-e^{-x}}\).
  • Aim: Evaluate \(g(x) = \int f(x)\, dx\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Integration by Substitution: Change variables to simplify the integrand.
  • Exponent Rule: \(e^{A+B} = e^A \cdot e^B \implies e^{-x-e^{-x}} = e^{-x} \cdot e^{-e^{-x}}\)
  • Standard Result: \( \displaystyle \int e^u\, du = e^u + C\)

4. Solution Method:

Rewrite the integral as \( \displaystyle \int e^{-x} \cdot e^{-e^{-x}}\, dx\), then use the substitution \(u = e^{-x}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Let \(u = e^{-x}\).
  2. Differentiate: \(\dfrac{du}{dx} = -e^{-x} \implies du = -e^{-x}\, dx \implies -du = e^{-x}\, dx\).
  3. Substitute:
    \[\int e^{-x} \cdot e^{-e^{-x}}\, dx = \int e^{-u}(-du) = -\int e^{-u}\, du \]
  4. Evaluate:
    \[-\int e^{-u}\, du = e^{-u} + C \]
  5. Substitute back \(u = e^{-x}\):
    \[g(x) = e^{-e^{-x}} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(e^{-e^{-x}}\)  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q20
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Consider the following partial differential equation:
\[3\dfrac{\partial^2 \phi}{\partial x^2} + B\dfrac{\partial^2 \phi}{\partial x \partial y} + 3\dfrac{\partial^2 \phi}{\partial y^2} + 4\phi = 0 \]
For this equation to be classified as parabolic, the value of \(B^2\) must be _______________
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Partial Differential Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: \(3\dfrac{\partial^2\phi}{\partial x^2} + B\dfrac{\partial^2\phi}{\partial x\partial y} + 3\dfrac{\partial^2\phi}{\partial y^2} + 4\phi = 0\)
  • Aim: Find the value of \(B^2\) for the equation to be parabolic.

3. Core Concepts:

For a second-order linear PDE of the form \(A\phi_{xx} + B\phi_{xy} + C\phi_{yy} + \ldots = 0\), the classification is based on the discriminant \(\Delta = B^2 - 4AC\):

  • Elliptic: \(B^2 - 4AC < 0\)
  • Parabolic: \(B^2 - 4AC = 0\)
  • Hyperbolic: \(B^2 - 4AC > 0\)

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify coefficients: \(A = 3\), \(C = 3\).
  2. Apply parabolic condition:
    \[B^2 - 4AC = 0 \implies B^2 - 4(3)(3) = 0 \implies B^2 = 36 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 36  |  Accepted key range: 35.9 to 36.1

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q21
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: \(\lim_{x \to 0} \left( \dfrac{\tan x}{x^2 - x} \right)\) is equal to _______________
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus (Limits)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: \(\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\tan x}{x^2 - x}\right)\)
  • Aim: Evaluate the limit.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Direct substitution gives \(0/0\) — indeterminate form.
  • Standard limit: \(\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\tan x}{x} = 1\)

4. Solution Method:

Factor the denominator as \(x(x-1)\), then split into the standard limit component and an algebraic component.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Factorize:
    \[\lim_{x\to 0}\dfrac{\tan x}{x(x-1)} = \lim_{x\to 0}\left(\dfrac{\tan x}{x} \cdot \dfrac{1}{x-1}\right) \]
  2. Apply product rule for limits:
    \[= \left(\lim_{x\to 0}\dfrac{\tan x}{x}\right) \times \left(\lim_{x\to 0}\dfrac{1}{x-1}\right) \]
  3. Evaluate each part:
    • \(\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}\dfrac{\tan x}{x} = 1\)
    • \(\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}\dfrac{1}{x-1} = \dfrac{1}{0-1} = -1\)
  4. Result: \(1 \times (-1) = -1\)

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: -1  |  Accepted key range: -1.1 to -0.9

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q26
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: For the function \(f(x)=a+bx\), \(0 \le x \le 1\), to be a valid probability density function, which one of the following statements is correct?
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability and Statistics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • A probability density function (PDF): \(f(x) = a + bx\)
    • Domain of the function: \(0 \le x \le 1\)
  • Aim: Identify the correct values of constants \(a\) and \(b\) from the given options that make \(f(x)\) a valid PDF.

3. Core Concepts:

For any continuous function \(f(x)\) to be a valid Probability Density Function (PDF) over an interval \([A, B]\), it must satisfy two fundamental conditions:

  • Non-negativity: The probability density cannot be negative.
    \[ f(x) \ge 0 \quad \text{for all } x \in [A, B] \]
  • Total Probability: The total area under the probability density curve must equal exactly 1.
    \[\int_{A}^{B} f(x) \, dx = 1 \]

4. Solution Method:

  • Apply the total probability condition by integrating the given function from 0 to 1 and equating it to 1. This gives a linear equation in terms of \(a\) and \(b\).
  • Test the given options against this equation.
  • Once an option satisfies the integration condition, verify it against the non-negativity condition.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Apply the total probability condition:
    \[\int_{0}^{1} (a + bx) \, dx = 1 \]\[ \left[ax + \dfrac{bx^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{1} = 1 \]\[a + \dfrac{b}{2} = 1 \implies 2a + b = 2 \]
  2. Check the given options against \(2a + b = 2\):
    Option\(a\)\(b\)\(2a + b\)Valid?
    A146✗
    B0.512✓
    C011✗
    D1-11✗
  3. Verify non-negativity for Option (B):
    Substituting \(a = 0.5,\ b = 1\): \(f(x) = 0.5 + x\)
    • At \(x = 0\): \(f(0) = 0.5 \ge 0\)
    • At \(x = 1\): \(f(1) = 1.5 \ge 0\)
    Since \(f(x)\) is strictly increasing and linear, \(f(x) \ge 0\) everywhere in the domain. Both conditions are met.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(a = 0.5,\ b = 1\)  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q27
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The solution of the equation \(\dfrac{dQ}{dt} + Q = 1\) with \(Q = 0\) at \(t = 0\) is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Ordinary Differential Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Linear ODE: \(\dfrac{dQ}{dt} + Q = 1\)
    • Initial Boundary Condition: \(Q = 0\) at \(t = 0\)
  • Aim: Find the particular solution \(Q(t)\) satisfying the ODE and the boundary condition.

3. Core Concepts:

The given equation is a first-order linear ODE of the standard form:

\[\dfrac{dy}{dt} + P(t)y = R(t) \]
  • Integrating Factor (IF): \(IF = e^{\int P(t)\, dt}\)
  • General Solution: \(y \times IF = \int (R(t) \times IF)\, dt + C\)

Alternatively, since variables are easily separable, the Variable Separable Method is used here.

4. Solution Method:

  • Rearrange to isolate \(Q\) terms on one side and \(t\) on the other.
  • Integrate both sides.
  • Apply the initial boundary condition to solve for the constant of integration \(C\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Separate the variables:
    \[\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = 1 - Q \implies \dfrac{dQ}{1 - Q} = dt \]
  2. Integrate both sides:
    \[\int \dfrac{1}{1 - Q}\, dQ = \int 1\, dt \]\[-\ln|1 - Q| = t + C \]
  3. Apply the initial condition \(Q(0) = 0\):
    \[-\ln|1 - 0| = 0 + C \implies -\ln(1) = C \implies C = 0 \]
  4. Formulate the final solution:
    \[-\ln(1 - Q) = t \implies \ln(1 - Q) = -t \]\[1 - Q = e^{-t} \implies Q(t) = 1 - e^{-t} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(Q(t) = 1 - e^{-t}\)  |  Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q28
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: Consider the matrix \(\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\). Which one of the following statements is TRUE for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of this matrix?
options: Eigenvalue 3 has a multiplicity of 2, and only one independent eigenvector exists.
Eigenvalue 3 has a multiplicity of 2, and two independent eigenvectors exist.
Eigenvalue 3 has a multiplicity of 2, and no independent eigenvector exists.
Eigenvalues are 3 and −3, and two independent eigenvectors exist.

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: Eigenvalue 3 has a multiplicity of 2, and only one independent eigenvector exists.
structuredOptions.html: Eigenvalue 3 has a multiplicity of 2, and only one independent eigenvector exists.

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: Eigenvalue 3 has a multiplicity of 2, and two independent eigenvectors exist.
structuredOptions.html: Eigenvalue 3 has a multiplicity of 2, and two independent eigenvectors exist.

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Eigenvalue 3 has a multiplicity of 2, and no independent eigenvector exists.
structuredOptions.html: Eigenvalue 3 has a multiplicity of 2, and no independent eigenvector exists.

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: Eigenvalues are 3 and −3, and two independent eigenvectors exist.
structuredOptions.html: Eigenvalues are 3 and −3, and two independent eigenvectors exist.

questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: A \(2 \times 2\) matrix \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\)
  • Aim: Determine the correct eigenvalues, their algebraic multiplicity, and the number of independent eigenvectors (geometric multiplicity).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Characteristic Equation: Found by \(|A - \lambda I| = 0\), where \(\lambda\) are the eigenvalues.
  • Algebraic Multiplicity: The number of times an eigenvalue appears as a root of the characteristic equation.
  • Geometric Multiplicity: Number of linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to an eigenvalue:
    \[\text{Geometric Multiplicity} = n - \text{Rank}(A - \lambda I) \]where \(n\) is the size of the square matrix.

4. Solution Method:

  • Derive the characteristic equation to find the eigenvalues.
  • Determine the algebraic multiplicity of the roots.
  • Substitute the eigenvalue into \((A - \lambda I)X = 0\) to find eigenvector(s).
  • Evaluate the rank of the resulting matrix to find the number of independent eigenvectors.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Find the eigenvalues:
    \[|A - \lambda I| = 0 \]\[\begin{vmatrix} 5 - \lambda & -1 \\ 4 & 1 - \lambda \end{vmatrix} = 0 \]\[(5 - \lambda)(1 - \lambda) + 4 = 0 \]\[\lambda^2 - 6\lambda + 9 = 0 \implies (\lambda - 3)^2 = 0 \implies \lambda = 3, 3 \]
    Eigenvalue \(\lambda = 3\) has an algebraic multiplicity of 2.
  2. Find the eigenvectors for \(\lambda = 3\):
    Solve \((A - 3I)X = 0\):
    \[\begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 4 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \]
    Row 2 is a multiple of Row 1, so there is only one independent equation: \(2x_1 - x_2 = 0 \implies x_2 = 2x_1\).
    Letting \(x_1 = k\), the eigenvector is \(X = k\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}\).
  3. Evaluate geometric multiplicity:
    \(\text{Rank}(A - 3I) = 1\)
    \[\text{Independent Eigenvectors} = n - \text{Rank} = 2 - 1 = 1 \]
    Thus, there is only one independent eigenvector for \(\lambda = 3\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Eigenvalue 3 has algebraic multiplicity 2, and only one independent eigenvector exists.  |  Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q37
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: Consider the equation \(\dfrac{du}{dt} = 3t^2 + 1\) with \(u = 0\) at \(t = 0\). This is numerically solved by using the forward Euler method with a step size, \(\Delta t = 2\). The absolute error in the solution at the end of the first time step is _______________
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods - Differential Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • ODE: \(\dfrac{du}{dt} = 3t^2 + 1\)
    • Initial condition: \(u(0) = 0\)
    • Numerical method: Forward Euler Method
    • Step size: \(\Delta t = 2\)
  • Aim: Find the absolute error in the solution at the end of the first time step (\(t = 2\)).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Exact (Analytical) Solution: Found by integrating the ODE using the initial boundary conditions.
  • Forward Euler Method: A first-order numerical procedure.
    \[u_{n+1} = u_n + f(t_n,\, u_n)\, \Delta t \]
  • Absolute Error: \(|\text{Exact Value} - \text{Approximate Value}|\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Integrate the ODE to find exact \(u(t)\); evaluate at \(t = 2\).
  2. Apply one iteration of the Forward Euler formula from \(t_0 = 0\) to find the numerical approximation at \(t = 2\).
  3. Calculate the absolute difference.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Exact Analytical Solution:
    \[\int du = \int (3t^2 + 1)\, dt \implies u(t) = t^3 + t + C \]Applying \(u(0) = 0\): \(C = 0\), so \(u(t) = t^3 + t\).
    At \(t = 2\):
    \[u_{exact}(2) = 2^3 + 2 = 10 \]
  2. Numerical Approximation (Euler's Method):
    \(f(t, u) = 3t^2 + 1\), \(\quad t_0 = 0\), \(\quad u_0 = 0\), \(\quad \Delta t = 2\)
    \[f(t_0, u_0) = 3(0)^2 + 1 = 1 \]\[u_1 = u_0 + f(t_0, u_0)\,\Delta t = 0 + (1)(2) = 2 \]
  3. Absolute Error:
    \[\text{Error} = |u_{exact} - u_{approx}| = |10 - 2| = 8 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 8.00  |  Accepted key range: 7.95 to 8.05

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q1
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Consider the following simultaneous equations (with \( c_1 \) and \( c_2 \) being constants):
\( 3x_1 + 2x_2 = c_1 \)
\( 4x_1 + x_2 = c_2 \)
The characteristic equation for these simultaneous equations is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Linear Algebra

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data: System of linear equations:
    \(3x_1 + 2x_2 = c_1\)
    \(4x_1 + x_2 = c_2\)
  • Aim: Find the characteristic equation for the given system.

3. Core Concepts:

A system of linear equations can be represented in matrix form as \(AX = C\), where \(A\) is the coefficient matrix. The characteristic equation of a square matrix \(A\) is given by \(|A - \lambda I| = 0\).

For a \(2 \times 2\) matrix, the standard shortcut formula is:\[\lambda^2 - \text{Trace}(A)\,\lambda + \text{Det}(A) = 0 \]

  • Trace(A): Sum of the principal diagonal elements.
  • Det(A): Determinant of the matrix.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Extract the coefficient matrix \(A\) from the equations.
  2. Calculate the Trace of the matrix.
  3. Calculate the Determinant of the matrix.
  4. Substitute both values into the characteristic equation formula.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Formulate the coefficient matrix \(A\):\[A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \]
  2. Calculate Trace(\(A\)):\[\text{Trace}(A) = 3 + 1 = 4 \]
  3. Calculate Det(\(A\)):\[\text{Det}(A) = (3)(1) - (2)(4) = 3 - 8 = -5 \]
  4. Construct the characteristic equation:\[\lambda^2 - (4)\lambda + (-5) = 0 \]\[\lambda^2 - 4\lambda - 5 = 0 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\lambda^2 - 4\lambda - 5 = 0\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q2
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: Let \( w = f(x, y) \), where \( x \) and \( y \) are functions of \( t \). Then, according to the chain rule, \( \dfrac{dw}{dt} \) is equal to
options: \( \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial x}\dfrac{\partial x}{\partial t} + \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial y}\dfrac{\partial y}{\partial t} \)

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: \( \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial x}\dfrac{\partial x}{\partial t} + \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial y}\dfrac{\partial y}{\partial t} \)
structuredOptions.html: \( \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial x}\dfrac{\partial x}{\partial t} + \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial y}\dfrac{\partial y}{\partial t} \)

questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus (Partial Derivatives)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Function \(w = f(x, y)\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are both functions of \(t\).
  • Aim: Determine the expression for the total derivative \(\dfrac{dw}{dt}\) using the chain rule.

3. Core Concepts:

When a dependent variable \(w\) relies on multiple intermediate variables (\(x\) and \(y\)), which are themselves governed by a single independent variable (\(t\)), the Multivariable Chain Rule dictates how rates of change propagate.

  • Because \(w\) depends on more than one variable, changes with respect to \(x\) and \(y\) require partial derivatives (\(\dfrac{\partial w}{\partial x}\) and \(\dfrac{\partial w}{\partial y}\)).
  • Because \(x\) and \(y\) depend on only one variable (\(t\)), changes with respect to \(t\) require ordinary derivatives (\(\dfrac{dx}{dt}\) and \(\dfrac{dy}{dt}\)).

4. Solution Method:

Write the total differential of \(w\), then divide through by \(dt\) to capture the rate of change with respect to \(t\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Total differential \(dw\):\[dw = \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial x}\,dx + \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial y}\,dy \]
  2. Divide by \(dt\):\[\dfrac{dw}{dt} = \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial x}\dfrac{dx}{dt} + \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial y}\dfrac{dy}{dt} \]

Common pitfall: Option B incorrectly uses partial derivatives for \(t\) (e.g., \(\dfrac{\partial x}{\partial t}\)). Since \(x\) and \(y\) are functions of \(t\) only, ordinary derivatives must be used.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{\partial w}{\partial x}\dfrac{dx}{dt} + \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial y}\dfrac{dy}{dt}\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q19
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The divergence of the vector field \( V = x^2 \mathbf{i} + 2y^3 \mathbf{j} + z^4 \mathbf{k} \) at \( x = 1 \), \( y = 2 \), \( z = 3 \) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Vector Calculus

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Vector field: \(\mathbf{V} = x^2\mathbf{i} + 2y^3\mathbf{j} + z^4\mathbf{k}\)
    • Point: \(x = 1,\ y = 2,\ z = 3\)
  • Aim: Find the divergence of \(\mathbf{V}\) at the given coordinates.

3. Core Concepts:

Divergence of a Vector Field:\[ abla \cdot \mathbf{V} = \dfrac{\partial V_x}{\partial x} + \dfrac{\partial V_y}{\partial y} + \dfrac{\partial V_z}{\partial z} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Identify the \(x\), \(y\), and \(z\) components of the vector field.
  2. Find the partial derivative of each component with respect to its variable.
  3. Sum the partial derivatives to get the general divergence expression.
  4. Substitute the point \((1, 2, 3)\) to find the numerical value.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Components: \(V_x = x^2\),   \(V_y = 2y^3\),   \(V_z = z^4\)
  2. Partial derivatives:
    \(\dfrac{\partial V_x}{\partial x} = 2x\),   \(\dfrac{\partial V_y}{\partial y} = 6y^2\),   \(\dfrac{\partial V_z}{\partial z} = 4z^3\)
  3. Divergence expression:\[ abla \cdot \mathbf{V} = 2x + 6y^2 + 4z^3 \]
  4. Substitute \(x=1,\ y=2,\ z=3\):\[ abla \cdot \mathbf{V} = 2(1) + 6(2)^2 + 4(3)^3 = 2 + 24 + 108 = 134 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 134 | Accepted key range: 133.9 to 134.1

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q20
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: A two-faced fair coin has its faces designated as head (H) and tail (T). This coin is tossed three times in succession to record the following outcomes: H, H, H. If the coin is tossed one more time, the probability (up to one decimal place) of obtaining H again, given the previous realizations of H, H and H, would be ___________
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability & Statistics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Fair coin (Head/Tail); past outcomes: H, H, H (3 tosses).
  • Aim: Determine the probability of getting a Head on the 4th toss.

3. Core Concepts:

Independent Events: A coin toss is a classic example of mutually independent events. The coin has no memory of previous tosses. For a fair coin, \(P(H) = 0.5\) for any individual toss, regardless of past history.

4. Solution Method:

Since past tosses have zero influence on the 4th toss, the conditional probability equals the marginal probability:\[P(H_{4th} \mid H_{1st}, H_{2nd}, H_{3rd}) = P(H) = 0.5 \]

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Confirm consecutive tosses are completely independent events.
  2. \(P(H) = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0.5\)
  3. The key insight: previous results (H, H, H) do not change this probability.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.5 | Accepted key range: 0.5 to 0.5

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q26
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question: The tangent to the curve represented by \( y = x \ln x \) is required to have 45° inclination with the x-axis. The coordinates of the tangent point would be
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Equation of the curve: \(y = x \ln x\)
    • Inclination of the tangent with the x-axis: \(\theta = 45^\circ\)
  • Aim: To find the coordinates of the tangent point \((x, y)\).

3. Core Concepts:

The slope \(m\) of a tangent to a curve \(y = f(x)\) at any point is given by its first derivative with respect to \(x\), i.e., \(m = \dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

The slope is also defined trigonometrically as \(m = \tan \theta\), where \(\theta\) is the angle of inclination of the tangent line with the positive x-axis.

Derivative product rule: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(u \cdot v) = u\dfrac{dv}{dx} + v\dfrac{du}{dx}\)

Standard derivative: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(\ln x) = \dfrac{1}{x}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute the derivative \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) for the function \(y = x \ln x\).
  2. Equate this derivative to the slope obtained from the given inclination, \(\tan(45^\circ)\).
  3. Solve the resulting algebraic equation to determine the x-coordinate of the point of tangency.
  4. Substitute the x-coordinate back into the original curve equation to find the corresponding y-coordinate.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Differentiate the curve equation
    Using the product rule on \(y = x \ln x\):\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}(\ln x) + \ln x \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}(x) \]\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) + \ln x \cdot (1) \]\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + \ln x \]
  2. Equate to the slope of the tangent
    Given inclination \(\theta = 45^\circ\), the slope is: \(m = \tan(45^\circ) = 1\)
    Setting \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = m\):\[1 + \ln x = 1 \]
  3. Solve for \(x\)\[\ln x = 0 \]Taking the exponential of both sides:\[x = e^0 = 1 \]
  4. Find the corresponding \(y\)-coordinate
    Substitute \(x = 1\) into \(y = x \ln x\):\[y = 1 \cdot \ln(1) = 1 \cdot 0 = 0 \]The coordinates of the tangent point are \((1, 0)\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \((1, 0)\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q27
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question:
Consider the following definite integral:
\[I = \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{(\sin^{-1} x)^2}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} dx \]
The value of the integral is
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Definite integral: \(I = \int_0^1 \dfrac{(\sin^{-1} x)^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\, dx\)
  • Aim: To evaluate the exact numerical value of the integral.

3. Core Concepts:

Integration by Substitution: When an integrand contains both a function and its derivative, substitution simplifies the integral.

Derivative of inverse trigonometric function: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin^{-1} x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\)

Power Rule for Integration: \(\int t^n\, dt = \dfrac{t^{n+1}}{n+1} + C\)

Definite Integrals: Limits of integration must be explicitly converted when substituting variables.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Identify that the derivative of \(\sin^{-1} x\) is exactly the \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\) present in the integrand.
  2. Apply the substitution \(t = \sin^{-1} x\) to convert the integral into a simple polynomial form.
  3. Calculate the new upper and lower limits with respect to \(t\).
  4. Integrate \(t^2\) and evaluate across the newly found limits.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Perform substitution
    Let \(t = \sin^{-1} x\). Differentiating with respect to \(x\):\[dt = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\, dx \]
  2. Update limits of integration
    For the lower limit, when \(x = 0\): \(t = \sin^{-1}(0) = 0\)
    For the upper limit, when \(x = 1\): \(t = \sin^{-1}(1) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\)
  3. Substitute and integrate
    Substitute \(t\), \(dt\), and the new limits into the integral:\[I = \int_0^{\pi/2} t^2\, dt \]Evaluate using the power rule:\[ I = \left[\dfrac{t^3}{3} \right]_0^{\pi/2} \]
  4. Evaluate bounds\[I = \dfrac{(\pi/2)^3}{3} - \dfrac{0^3}{3} = \dfrac{\pi^3/8}{3} = \dfrac{\pi^3}{24} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{\pi^3}{24}\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q28
